386YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: Thirteen territories elected senators, among them Éamon Ashenmourn de Cordraco for Astolat, Rane Shardbearer for Kallavesa and Herminius of the House of the Wanderer for Zenith. The Senate appointed ambassadors to Axos, Jarm, the Grendel and the Iron Confederacy, eight generals and many title-holders, including the Grimnir of Wittal Grove. The Synod chose Luca i Taziel i Riqueza as Cardinal of Prosperity with 258 votes and Tabris, Son of Armisael, as Cardinal of the Way. The Military Council named strategoi for Highguard and Navarr. Bourse auctions and votes allocated numerous seats, such as Master of Rings, which went to Laughlan Vi Temeschwar with 680 votes.

n.Dawn: Dawn's territories of Astolat and Weirwater gained new senators: Éamon Ashenmourn de Cordraco and Tristan du Lac respectively.
n.Grendel: Garviel i Abrira i Erigo was elected Senator for Feroz, a territory Grendel held that season, and the Senate appointed Finna as Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Kish of the Flame Beneath the Earth became Senator for Necropolis, and the Military Council appointed Arlandria of the Sentinels Tower as Strategos of Highguard.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs' territory.
n.Jotun: Willem Tarne was elected Senator for Bregasland, a territory the Jotun held that season.
n.Navarr: Rowyn of the Waystone Path became Senator for Hercynia, and the Military Council appointed Gryiff Embercast as Strategos of Navarr.
n.The League: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar, the League's territory.
n.The Marches: Hal Talbot was elected Senator for Mitwold, the Marcher territory.
n.Urizen: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer was elected Senator for Zenith, the Urizen territory.
n.Varushka: Varushka's two territories gained senators: Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti for Miekarova and Velko Perunovich Razoradze for Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Rane Shardbearer was elected Senator for Kallavesa, and Theowold Vakarsson was appointed Grimnir of Wittal Grove.

t.Astolat: Éamon Ashenmourn de Cordraco was elected Senator for Astolat.
t.Bregasland: Willem Tarne was elected Senator for Bregasland while the territory was held by the Jotun.
t.Feroz: Garviel i Abrira i Erigo was elected Senator for Feroz while the territory was held by Grendel.
t.Hercynia: Rowyn of the Waystone Path was elected Senator for Hercynia.
t.Kallavesa: Rane Shardbearer was elected Senator for Kallavesa, and the territory's Wittal Grove received a new Grimnir.
t.Miekarova: Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti was elected Senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: Hal Talbot was elected Senator for Mitwold.
t.Necropolis: Kish of the Flame Beneath the Earth was elected Senator for Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Velko Perunovich Razoradze was elected Senator for Ossium.
t.Skarsind: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar.
t.Weirwater: Tristan du Lac was elected Senator for Weirwater, and Bartimaeus won the Weirwater Vales title at Bourse auction for 250 thrones.
t.Zenith: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer was elected Senator for Zenith.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Senate appointed Theowold Vakarsson as Grimnir of Wittal Grove.

386YE Winter Solstice Military Council o.d: The accompanying wind, Rippling Stones, reported that Jarl Haakon was dead in the Mournwold, though his champions fought on. The Druj held eastern Therunin, and Grendel navies had been routed from Redoubt. The Children of Wrecks' Gathered Storm lay in Free Landing, threatening the Bay of Catazar. After the Senate rejected a peace treaty, the Autumn Hammers, Summer Storm, Bounders, Bloodcloaks and Fist of the Mountains crossed into Reinos. The Winter Sun, Towerjacks, Golden Axe and Citadel Guard struck the Sarangrave, the Citadel Guard under Winter's Mantle. The Drakes and Tusks pressed on into the Ore Hills. Only the Summer Storm and Golden Axe would see their supporting units share the guerdon.

n.Dawn: All three Dawn armies gathered in Astolat to defend and resupply. The Gryphon's Pride left Bitter Strand under orders to let the Rahvin go home, and the Eastern Sky held an arcane consolidation.
n.Druj: The Druj held eastern Therunin, but four Imperial armies struck into the Sarangrave to break the Mallum and threaten any Druj forces left in Therunin.
n.Grendel: Grendel navies had been routed from Redoubt and forced back to sea, though the wind stressed they were not defeated.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar resupplied in Astolat, while the Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus billeted on the Marchers in Upwold to rest after a year of crusade.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Autumn Hammers and Summer Storm attacked Reinos, the Hammers plundering and the Summer Storm earning the guerdon. The Winter Sun began a steady conquest of Bloodwater Marsh in the Sarangrave.
n.Jotun: With Jarl Haakon dead, Jotun champions still fought in the Mournwold while the bulk of their armies waited in Liathaven. After the Senate rejected peace, five Imperial armies invaded Reinos.
n.Navarr: Both Navarr armies went to Reikos: the Black Thorns reinforced it while aiding kin evacuating from Therunin, and the Quiet Step mounted a solid defence.
n.The Brass Coast: The Burning Falcon and Red Wind Corsairs defended Tassato and the Fire of the South held Astolat, while allied armies invaded Reinos partly to protect the freeborn.
n.The League: The Towerjacks joined the Sarangrave offensive, seeking allies among the Druj-ruled people there, while the Wolves of War withdrew to rest in Astolat.
n.The Marches: The Drakes and Tusks pressed a steady conquest into the Ore Hills after Haakon's death. The Bounders advanced into Reinos via Burnish, and the Strong Reeds lay low in Bregasland, amid early rumblings of dissent over new exemplars.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the wind notes that time is running out on the treaty with the orcs of Otkodov.
n.Urizen: Urizen's coast was still lashed by storms after the Redoubt raid, and its Citadel Guard crossed into the Sarangrave wrapped in Winter's Mantle.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe led the charge to take land in the Sarangrave and earned the guerdon, while the Northern Eagle went to Astolat to rest and grieve.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and the Fist of the Mountains, the latter enchanted with Quickening Cold Meat, invaded Reinos, while the Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear billeted in Upwold.

t.Astolat: Seven Imperial armies gathered in Astolat to defend, resupply and rest, among them three from Dawn, the Granite Pillar, the Fire of the South, the Wolves of War and the Northern Eagle.
t.Bay of Catazar: At least half the Bay of Catazar was judged to lie within reach of the Children of Wrecks' Gathered Storm, which was expected to strike next in full force.
t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds lay low in the Bregasland marshes, harrying Jotun remnants and guarding against Gravenmarch.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War's general recalled that the army had stormed Feroz.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the southern and northern Jotun armies, including the Hierro and Corazón, had withdrawn to the eaves of Liathaven.
t.Madruga: The Children of Wrecks' Gathered Storm, a full navy backed by pirates, was believed to be in Free Landing, though unlikely to stay.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun set out from Mareave for the Sarangrave.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step left Miaren for Reikos, and the Wolves of War marched through it on their way to Astolat.
t.Mournwold: Jarl Haakon was dead, and the Drakes and Tusks stayed to drive his remaining champions from the Ore Hills. Several other armies left the territory.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the wind notes that the sands are running fast on the treaty with the orcs of Otkodov.
t.Redoubt: Grendel navies were routed from Redoubt and only one of the traitors who led the raid was found, dead on the battlefield. Storms and flash floods continued, but Visten endured.
t.Reikos: The Navarr armies Black Thorns and Quiet Step took up position in Reikos to reinforce, defend and aid kin evacuating from Therunin.
t.Reinos: Five Imperial armies invaded Reinos after the Senate rejected the peace treaty, facing fortified passes and the castles of Getshal and Yegarra's Proof.
t.Sarangrave: The Winter Sun, Towerjacks, Golden Axe and Citadel Guard crossed into the Sarangrave to break the Mallum, under the shadow of the Tower of the Skink.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders' route into Reinos ran through Burnish in Segura.
t.Tassato: The Burning Falcon and Red Wind Corsairs mounted a solid defence of Tassato, where the dead were said to rise alongside the Fist of the Mountains.
t.The Barrens: The Gryphon's Pride quit the Fangs and left Bitter Strand to let the Rahvin go home, and the Barrens' Dawn armies withdrew to Astolat.
t.Therunin: Druj armies held the east of Therunin after heavy Imperial losses. The Golden Sun and Black Thorns withdrew as Navarr kin evacuated, and the Sarangrave attack aimed to cut off the Druj remaining there.
t.Upwold: Four armies billeted in Upwold on Marcher hospitality: the Seventh Wave, Valiant Pegasus, Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe marched from Zenith to the Sarangrave.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Bregasland were described as guarding against Gravenmarch.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Gathered Storm, a full navy backed by pirates and murderers, was believed to be anchored at Free Landing.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Drakes and Tusks advanced into the Ore Hills to clear out the Jotun and rebuild after Haakon's death.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: The Winter Sun began a steady conquest into Bloodwater Marsh, seeking to make its first mark on the Sarangrave.
r.Segura/Burnish: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders marched through Burnish on their way into Reinos.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Gryphon's Pride withdrew from Bitter Strand to let the Rahvin go home and to block any who would prevent them.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: East Ashes remained in Druj hands as part of their hold on eastern Therunin.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: The wind warned that nothing stood between the Druj Ghulai and the warped secrets of the Greenheart.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Mentioned in passing: the wind speaks only of a valley the Druj poisoned with their own corrupted apothecary, without naming the region directly.

386YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: The Senate abrogated the Imperial Administrator and created the Stipulator of Stipends, to which Benedict Urban Di Tassato was elected. He then cut the High Exorcist's stipend to four thrones. Tolls on the Blood Red and White Roads will bring in an extra hundred thrones a season, while broader road tolls and the Lasambrian treaty failed. A third Navarr army was rejected. Commissions passed included a citadel in Peregro, the Gallery of Memories and a remodelled Virtue's Rest. Title-holders announced further works, among them Sergio's Kitchen and improvements to the Great Chain in Sarvos and a timbermill in Temeschwar. Several ambassadors were elected, and Empress Vesna drew 227 thrones through the Hand of the Chancellor.

n.Dawn: Bitter Strand in the Barrens, including the Fangs mithril mine, was ceded to the Rahvin sept, and the Fangs could be allocated as a Dawnish national seat. Finna of Dawn was re-elected Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Druj: The Imperial Apothecaries Guild was instructed to spread an antidote to the Druj poison in Therunin's Lower Tarn Valley. A citadel was commissioned in Peregro to watch the Therunin border, where the Druj hold sway.
n.Grendel: Finna of Dawn, the incumbent, was re-elected as the Empire's Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Virtue's Rest is to be remodelled to help soldiers of the War of Thorns and Flowers recover, with its Exarch elected by the Highborn assembly. A Church of the Roads sinecure was announced in Bastion, appointed by the Highguard National Assembly.
n.Navarr: The motion to raise a third Navarr army in Hercynia failed. Micah's Stand wayhouse was commissioned in Reikos, and Navarri citizens were elected Ambassador to Axos and Captain of the Senate Guard.
n.The League: The Senate allowed a third League army to be raised, and Benedict Urban Di Tassato became the first Stipulator of Stipends. League works were announced in Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar, while the Tassatan Hills bourse amendment was withdrawn.
n.The Marches: Mournwold was assigned to the Marches, with its senator to be elected at the Spring Equinox 387YE. Marcher farm owners will be able to drive cattle to market for cattle-bonds under the new Shepherd of the Southern Herd.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Xanthius of Urizen was elected Guildmaster of the Artisans, and Urizeni senators proposed or seconded several motions.
n.Varushka: A third Varushkan army is to be raised, and an appraisal will look at drawing displaced Varushkans to Delev. The Gallery of Memories was commissioned in Ossium, with its Curator appointed by the Varushkan National Assembly.

t.Mournwold: The Senate assigned Mournwold to the Marches, and the election for its senator will take place at the Spring Equinox 387YE.
t.Sarvos: Sergio's Kitchen was announced as a League sinecure in Cigno, and an improvement to the Great Chain fortification was announced, its cost yet to be determined.
t.Temeschwar: The Temeschwar Drovers' Guild Timbermill and Sorting Yard was announced as a great work in Vardstein Vale. The Temeschwar senator also secured the Torch Eternal as regalia for the Watcher of Ratibor's Torch.
t.The Barrens: The Senate ceded Bitter Strand, including the Fangs mithril mine, to the Rahvin sept. A motion was raised to allocate the Fangs, now claimed by the Empire.

r.Sarvos/Cigno: Cigno will host the new sinecure of Sergio's Kitchen, and its Great Chain fortification is to be improved.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: A timbermill and sorting yard is to be built here, creating the Vardstein Vandal to oversee the vale's resources and its wolves.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Bitter Strand, with the Fangs mithril mine, was ceded to the Rahvin sept by vote of the Senate.

386YE Winter Solstice Synod judgements.d: The General Assembly excommunicated Archavion Wolfborne, and the Dawnish Assembly revoked him as General of the Gryphon's Pride. A Dawnish veto of the ceding of the Fangs failed, while the General Assembly urged returning the mine to the Rahvin. Zoran de Orzel and Spymaster Bernard Dugdale were revoked. Viviane Barossa resigned as Cardinal of Ambition. Assemblies across the Empire offered refuge to Navarr and Great Forest Orcs fleeing Therunin. Other judgements condemned cruel armies, warned of the Children of Wrecks, Agramant's cults and the Claw, backed dams in Spiral, and recognised several exemplars. Mandates sent priests to Solokha, Asavea and Astolat, and true liao consecrated Hacynian and Capodomus.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly revoked Archavion Wolfborne as General of the Gryphon's Pride and condemned his name to infamy, though its veto of the ceding of the Fangs failed. It also urged the nation to help rebuild Drycastle, proposed a Test of Devotion and opened the Barrens to refugees from Therunin.
n.Druj: The Druj conquest of Therunin drove Navarr and Great Forest Orcs to flee into neighbouring nations. The Navarr Assembly committed to the Druj's destruction, and the Highborn urged defence of the Reikos–Therunin border.
n.Grendel: The General Assembly urged citizens of the southern shores to prepare against the Grendel's return, and the Assembly of Nine castigated over Pickers Goldleaf's admitted treason with the Grendel. The Prosperity Assembly demanded fair pay for labourers in Grendel-held Feroz.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly pledged further Peerless Kinship, opened Reikos to refugees from Therunin and warned that Siakha will attack Necropolis. It also declared 387YE the year of certainty, and a penance sought to heal the feud that split Highborn forces at the Autumn battle.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly asked to send bonetenders to recover and name their dead at Solen's Doubt in any Spiral dam. It mandated the Sunstorm sept to aid Feroz and revoked MemoryKeeper Ikhan's title.
n.Jotun: The Freeborn Assembly vowed to veto any ceding of Segura under the proposed Lasambrian treaty, which the Senate rejected. The Marcher Assembly called for repairing Fisher's Rock against the Jotun.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly urged Therunin's people to fight as guerrillas or seek refuge and committed to destroying the Druj. It mourned Isaella's Dance, sought to preserve Thornbound knowledge, and backed a fane to Arhallogen for the war on the vallorn. A bid to revoke Rhisiart Dancewalker failed.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly vowed to veto any ceding of Segura and called for Siroc to be rebuilt in Madruga. It also urged that all Freeborn senatorial election bids be kept by the nation.
n.The League: The League Assembly endorsed the Chamber of Eyphony in Spiral, backed damming the river Doubt for its fallen, and welcomed Commonwealth visitors. It also announced Holberg's 250th anniversary celebration and warned of Agramant cultists in Holberg and a traitor threatening Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly called on Marchers to repair Fisher's Rock and stood with the Mournwold miners, and the leaders of the Ore Hills rebellion were recognised as exemplars of Pride. It exalted Gerraint Black and warned against the Husks of the Deep on the Gullet coast.
n.Thule: The Courage Assembly urged that negotiations with the Thule proceed as the Otkodov ceasefire ends, to avoid renewed war on the northern border. The Varushkan Assembly cited the Thule in calling for the Volodmartz citadel to be funded.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly opened its spires to refugees from Therunin and warned Redoubt to prepare for the storms of Siakha's cultists. It also urged support for anchoring the Way in Asavea and vigilance over the cattle drive through Spiral.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly backed a warded reservoir over its fallen in Spiral and confirmed that Empress Vesna has no ties to Blood on Snow. It also warned of husks and of the traitor Zavetta Voglanova, and the Navarr honoured the sacrifice of the Iron Helms. Its call to destroy the Orieb shrines failed.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly backed a fane to Sadogua over Kallavesa, added Kali Keeneye and Gisli the Provider to the Chronicle of Heroes, and welcomed the Great Forest Orcs. It castigated Lodwick Hardin over the attack on the Rahvin, but its support for Navarr's vallorn plan failed.

t.Bastion: Judgements urged continued work on the Grand Inspiration of the Way and affirmed the hostels of Virtue's Rest as places to restore both body and soul. Marcher monasteries were asked to go to Bastion and take on work the Lepidean librarians would not.
t.Bregasland: The Marcher Assembly lamented that Bregasland has been left unfortified and called on all Marchers to give coin, labour and resources to repair Fisher's Rock.
t.Feroz: The Prosperity Assembly warned those commissioning work in impoverished Feroz to pay its labourers fairly. An Imperial Orc mandate asked the Sunstorm sept to aid Feroz, though they have not yet set out because the Icarion Qanat was not commissioned.
t.Holberg: The League Assembly named Holberg as the hub of Agramant's cannibal cults and called for the sect to be rooted out. It also announced a grand celebration of 250 years since Holberg joined the Empire.
t.Kallavesa: The Wintermark Assembly supported casting an arcane projection over Kallavesa as part of the oath for a fane to Sadogua, sought by the Ravenseer to protect the territory.
t.Madruga: The Navarr Assembly urged its people to help the Freeborn adapt to the strange new marshes rising in Madruga, and the Freeborn Assembly called for Siroc to be rebuilt there once reclaimed. Bakar was vindicated over his choices during the flooding.
t.Mareave: The Prosperity Assembly warned against expanding the Yellow Fist Adit to take water from Skouran Jadefall. Urizeni priests urged vigilance over a planned cattle drive to Mareave through Spiral.
t.Necropolis: Both the Highborn and Vigilance Assemblies warned that Siakha's Children of Wrecks will attack Necropolis next season and called for its defence.
t.Redoubt: The Urizen Assembly warned Redoubt to prepare for storms brought by Siakha's cultists and to shelter with neighbours if needed. Other judgements recalled the Children of Wrecks raid there and condemned Imperials who aided it.
t.Reikos: The Highborn Assembly asked Reikos's chapters to shelter Navarr and Great Forest Orc refugees and called for the Reikos–Therunin border to be defended against the Druj.
t.Spiral: Assemblies endorsed building the Chamber of Eyphony in Spiral and backed damming the river Doubt. The Imperial Orc and Varushkan Assemblies asked that their fallen at Solen's Doubt be honoured, and Urizen urged vigilance over the coming cattle drive through Spiral.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: donations made at Tassato's counting house added two thrones to the Virtue Fund.
t.The Barrens: Archavion Wolfborne was excommunicated and revoked for attacking the Rahvin at the Fangs, the veto of ceding the Fangs failed, and the General Assembly urged returning the mine. The Dawnish Assembly also opened the Barrens to Therunin's refugees and urged the rebuilding of Drycastle.
t.Therunin: With Therunin falling to the Druj, the Navarr Assembly urged those who could not fight to flee and those who could to harass the invaders. Urizen, Dawn and Highguard opened their doors to Navarr and Great Forest Orc refugees.

r.Mareave/Icarion: The Icarion Qanat was not commissioned at the Winter Solstice, so the Sunstorm sept has not yet set out to aid Feroz. They will go if it is commissioned before the end of the Autumn Equinox 387YE.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Navarr Assembly urged travellers to show the Karass sept that the Last Battle wayhouse in the Bleaks stands against the Druj, not against them.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Navarr Assembly praised Thornsong House and urged that its knowledge be spread along the trods. A later judgement called for its work to be carried to safety from the Druj.

386YE Winter Solstice event schedule.d: Ten nations were scheduled to elect senators in their camps on Saturday afternoon, each by its own method. Tally of the Votes elections for numerous national titles followed from 3:30pm. Senate sessions were set for Friday at 10pm, Saturday at 4pm and 9pm, and Sunday at 1:30pm. The Military Council would sit on Saturday and Sunday, with battles off Anvil at 11am both days. The Hall of Worlds was to host Conclave sessions, Grandmaster elections and parleys with Meraud and Sorin. The schedule also included an auction for Imperial Bourse positions, trials of four individuals for blasphemy and heresy, and regular Synod judgement deadlines.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senators for Astolat and Weirwater were to be chosen at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney, and Dawnish Fleet Captains were to meet in the Military Council tent at 1pm on Saturday.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the Feroz senatorial seat is listed as a Brass Coast auction election.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis senator election was to open with the inquisition of candidates at 2pm.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were to elect Skarsind's senator from 2:15pm as candidates presented items of worth. At 4pm at the Fire Pit they would elect the Keeper of the Bronze Bowls, the Steward of the Mines of Gulhule and the Four Seasons' Boneweaver.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the Bregasland senatorial seat is listed among the Marches elections.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were to elect Hercynia's senator at 1:15pm, immediately after the standing, and to elect the Broker of the Invisible Cord at the Standing Circle at 4:30pm.
n.The League: The League's Temeschwar senator election was to begin at 3:30pm with the presentation of collected bonds. The Master of Rings and the Chair of the Wolf were to be elected at the Plaza at 5pm.
n.The Marches: Marcher landowners were to gather at 1:30pm to elect senators for Bregasland and Mitwold. At 5pm at the Community Hall the Marches would elect the Steward of Good Leaf Gardens, the Bailiff of the Grand Market and the Reeve of the Happiston Mana Exchange.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Zenith senator was to be chosen by a demos running from 1pm to 2pm. The Gloaming Merchant and the Architect of the Conscious River were to be elected near the Net of Heaven at 3:30pm, and the nation's magicians were to meet on Friday evening.
n.Varushka: Varushka's senator elections for Ossium and Miekarova were to begin with questioning of candidates at 1:45pm. At 4pm at the Central Hearth it would elect five titles, among them the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak and the Speaker to the Leshun.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Kallavesa senator election was to begin at 2pm, with jars placed down for 30 minutes.

t.Astolat: Astolat's senator was to be chosen in the Dawnish camp at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland's senator election is listed under the Marches, with landowners gathering at 1:30pm.
t.Feroz: The Feroz senator election is listed as a Brass Coast auction beginning at 2pm. The next regular election for the seat is due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia's senator was to be elected in the Navarr camp at 1:15pm, immediately after the standing.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator was to be chosen from 2pm, with Wintermark's jars placed down for 30 minutes.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's senator election was to begin with questioning of candidates in the Varushkan camp at 1:45pm.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold's senator was to be elected by Marcher landowners from 1:30pm. The next regular election for the seat is due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis's senator election was to open with the Highborn inquisition of candidates at 2pm.
t.Ossium: Ossium's senator election was to begin with questioning of candidates in the Varushkan camp at 1:45pm.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind's senator election was to begin at 2:15pm, with Imperial Orc candidates presenting items of worth.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's senator election was to begin at 3:30pm with the presentation of collected bonds in the League camp.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater's senator was to be chosen in the Dawnish camp at 2:30pm, after the tourney. The next regular election for the seat is due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.
t.Zenith: Zenith's senator was to be chosen by a Urizen demos running from 1pm to 2pm.

386YE Winter Solstice interlude.d: General Archavion Wolfborne ordered the Gryphon's Pride to seize the Fangs mithril mine from the Rahvin, whom the Senate had declared foreigners. Supporting the army would mean a murder trial. A Save the Rahvin adventure could spare the sept if units with a combined strength of 2,000 joined it. Other adventures covered exploring transformed southern Madruga and the Untrod Groves. Robec began offering Kobol's Vigour, and the Iron Confederacy lifted its sanctions. Further effects included farmers travelling to Mareave, Temeschwar priests sheltering the needy, Sorin's boon in Hahnmark, curses on Redoubt, Summer magic over Dawn, Regrow the Land's Heart on Upwold and Feroz, and a Penumbral Veil over every Imperial territory except Casinea.

n.Dawn: A Dawnish army, the Gryphon's Pride, was marching illegally on the Rahvin in the Barrens, and Dawnish knights could explore the Untrod Groves. The whole nation was enchanted with Summer magic that draws Summer eternals and stirs a love of showy magic.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the attack on the Rahvin was expected to damage future chances of the Empire cooperating with the slaves of the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, though Feroz and Mareave, listed here as Grendel-held, are treated on the page as Imperial lands receiving magic and aid.
n.Highguard: The consecrated basilica of Berechiah in Bastion still gave Vigilance preachers extra liao and votes. The Penumbral Veil covered Bastion, Necropolis and Reikos but conspicuously not Casinea.
n.Imperial Orcs: Brass Coast and Marcher farmers were trekking to Mareave to help the Imperial Orcs cope with the arid conditions of their new territory. The Penumbral Veil covered both Mareave and Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Penumbral Veil covered only those Marcher lands where the Jotun were not in control.
n.Navarr: The Penumbral Veil was drawn over Miaren and Hercynia, the two territories still held by the nation.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast congregations lost a liao and two Synod votes as their farmers travelled to aid the Orcs. Military units could explore the flood-transformed south of Madruga, and the Veil covered Kahraman, Segura and Feroz.
n.The League: Temeschwar priests preaching Vigilance or Loyalty gained votes but lost liao while sheltering those troubled by the rat-plague. The Veil covered all five cities, and over Sarvos it was more than three times as strong.
n.The Marches: Congregations in Mitwold and Upwold lost a liao and two votes as farmers trekked to Mareave. Upwold was enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart, and the Veil covered the Marcher lands outside Jotun control.
n.Urizen: Redoubt was cursed with Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea, which cut fleet production, and with Rivers of Life. The Veil covered all three Urizen territories.
n.Varushka: Fleets crossing the Semmerlak from Varushka were no longer penalised, thanks to the journeymage towers. The Veil covered all five Varushkan territories.
n.Wintermark: Sorin's boon strengthened Hahnmark's herb gardens, and Sermersuaq's personal resources gained 22 extra rings. The Veil covered all three Wintermark territories.

t.Astolat: Astolat lay under the Summer enchantment covering all of Dawn and under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Bastion: The consecrated but still dangerous basilica of Berechiah continued to inspire Vigilance preachers, and Bastion was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: farmers were trekking around the Bay to Mareave, and the eternal Siakha's growing influence over it could affect the Redoubt curse.
t.Bregasland: The page listed Bregasland among the Marcher territories covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Casinea: Casinea was the only Imperial territory left out of the Penumbral Veil, a pointed exception suggesting dozens of deliberate castings.
t.Feroz: The reclaimed Feroz was enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart, bringing soft rain, new growth over war scars and more briar births. It was also covered by the Veil.
t.Hahnmark: Heralds of Sorin culled the weak plants in Hahnmark's herb gardens, adding herbs and bladeroot. Residents felt possessive and suspicious of strangers, and the eternal's price was unknown.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia, still held by Navarr, was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Holberg: Fleets crossing the Semmerlak from Holberg no longer suffered a production penalty, and the city lay under the Veil.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was covered by the Penumbral Veil, and its congregations were among those losing liao and votes as farmers left to aid the Orcs.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Karov: Karov was covered by the Penumbral Veil, and Varushkan fleets crossing the Semmerlak were no longer penalised.
t.Karsk: Karsk was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Madruga: Military units could take the Explore the Southern Reaches adventure in the flood-reshaped south of Madruga. If 5,000 strength was committed in one season, the Empire could remap the territory and scry it again.
t.Mareave: Brass Coast and Marcher farmers were travelling to Mareave to help the Imperial Orcs deal with its arid conditions, and the territory was covered by the Veil.
t.Miaren: Miaren, still held by Navarr, was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Mitwold: Congregations in Mitwold lost a liao and two Synod votes as their farmers trekked to Mareave, and the territory lay under the Veil.
t.Morrow: Morrow was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Ossium: Ossium was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was battered by the storms of Foam and Spittle of the Furious Sea, which cut fleet production by two ranks, and was also under the opposing Rivers of Life curse. The full consequences were left to the Winter winds.
t.Reikos: Reikos was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Sarvos: The Penumbral Veil over Sarvos was more than three times as powerful as elsewhere in the Empire.
t.Segura: Segura was covered by the Penumbral Veil, and its congregations were among those losing liao and votes as farmers left to aid the Orcs.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm lay under Dawn's Summer enchantment and the Penumbral Veil, and fleets crossing the Semmerlak from Dawn were no longer penalised.
t.Sermersuaq: Having defied a harsh winter and Agramant's schemes, Sermersuaq's people prospered, and every personal resource there produced an extra 22 rings.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Spiral: Spiral was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Tassato: Tassato was covered by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's churches opened to those suffering from the rat-plague. Priests preaching Vigilance or Loyalty gained two votes but spent a liao on consecrations for the needy.
t.The Barrens: The Gryphon's Pride was attacking the Rahvin to seize the Fangs mithril mine, and the Houndsgate fortification would not oppose it. The sept could survive, though it would lose the mine, if units with 2,000 combined strength came to its aid.
t.The Semmerlak: Journeymage towers lessened Dho'uala's influence, so fleets crossing the lake were no longer penalised. Removing things from the Semmerlak remained illegal, and the Harbourmaster still could not buy ilium.
t.Upwold: Upwold was enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart, its congregations lost liao and votes to the farmers' trek, and it lay under the Veil.
t.Veroigne: The Duke of Veroigne lifted the ban on selling Kobol's Vigour to Imperial traders at Robec, and the Iron Dukes ended their sanctions, though trade in Veroigne still faced delays and scrutiny.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater lay under Dawn's Summer enchantment and the Penumbral Veil.
t.Zenith: Zenith was covered by the Penumbral Veil.

r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Mentioned in passing: Lacuve is not named; it shares only in the Summer enchantment and Veil over Semmerholm.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Dawnish knights could send military units to explore the Untrod Groves for wealth, with reports promised if 1,000 strength or more was sent. The enchanted fortification summoned there would not stop the Gryphon's Pride's attack.

386YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: Emperor Vesna addressed all citizens about the Barrens, where the attack on the Rahvin divided Dawn and the Fangs passed to Imperial control. Highguard, the League and Varushka began preparing to support the Navarr against the vallorn. Senate appraisals examined Feroz and the Grendel salt lords, and a treaty with the Lasambrian Orcs awaited a constitutional vote. Four Synod cardinals faced heresy trial over an aura of Peace. The Thule warned of war after Summer 387YE without agreement. Madruga was transformed by marsh, Mareave's development was discussed, and twenty-three normal and three major conjunctions were resolved, mostly in the Empire's favour.

n.Dawn: Dawn was polarised over General Achavion Wolfborne's attack on the Rahvin, while questing knights prepared an expedition into the Untrod Groves and Imperial heroes killed Druj ritualists there and the Speakers of Famine in Astolat.
n.Druj: The Druj suffered defeats in Therunin, Morrow and the Barrens, with the Blood Drainers coven and Cintra Blackstaff stopped in Sweetglades and the Shuddering Wrast slain.
n.Grendel: An appraisal studied ways to disrupt the Salt Lords Council and its allies, the damage left by Governor Rahab in Feroz was assessed, and Grendel forces were killed at Ayereed, Sarvos and Kallavesa.
n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims used their final peerless kinship to seek healing for Therunin, the grey pilgrims were called home to raise an army against the vallorn, and ghosts gathered at High Chalcis in Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation's people weighed ways to bring water and prosperity to arid Mareave and plan for a possible Grendel return, and were approached by emissaries of the Autumn realm.
n.Jotun: Jotun warbands were beaten across Mournwold, Tassato and Bregasland, losing their last cache in Southmoor, though Liath's Ring gained the under threat quality.
n.Navarr: Highborn pilgrims worked with the Navarr on Therunin's ghosts and taint, three nations rallied to their war on the vallorn, the vine movement found its purpose, and a new wayhouse was completed in the Bleaks.
n.The Brass Coast: A peace treaty with the Lasambrian Orcs awaited Senate approval, an appraisal proposed measures for ruined Feroz, and Madruga was transformed into marsh while the Children of Wrecks formed a navy.
n.The League: The League set its innovators to study the vallorn, the Assembly of Ambition sought true consecration of Capodomus Cathedral, and Imperial heroes protected Holberg, Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: Marchers were stirred by the Pride assembly seeking recognition for the Ore Hills Rebellion ringleaders and the revocation of a Marcher senator, while the Miners of the Mourn were rescued in the Ore Hills.
n.Thule: The long peace with the Thule was close to ending, with war due after the Summer Solstice 387YE if no agreement is reached.
n.Urizen: Former Urizen renegades in Ankra began attacking Imperial citizens, Urizen was tagged in developments in Mareave, and the Shuddering Wrast was killed in Morrow.
n.Varushka: The Varushkans sought to draw on dark powers against the vallorn, the wolves of Nadezhdikov were soothed in Volodmartz, and Bulgakov in Karov was made habitable.
n.Wintermark: The Icebarn artok, bound by runes, awaited new tasks for Wintermark, beasts grew wild in Sermersuaq, and heroes killed the Crimson Band in Hahnmark and guarded the Pilgrim's Trail in Kallavesa.

t.Astolat: The Speakers of Famine were all killed at the Grand Spinney in Winterbourne.
t.Ayereed: Imperial heroes stopped the Asaveans reinforcing Stormlords Rise, killing them and the Grendel and claiming a chest.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, though the page touches on Imperial fleets and overseas trade.
t.Bregasland: The Jotun were defeated at Hal's Hollow and the Feni protected from slaughter.
t.Brocéliande: An emissary of the Green Mother offered a boon to remove the malign curse over Brocéliande, though accepting any of her boons is illegal.
t.Feroz: A Senate appraisal presented proposals for ruined Feroz and began assessing the damage done by Grendel Governor Rahab.
t.Hahnmark: The Crimson Band were all killed at the Tainted Bawn, and Hahnmark farmers were tagged in Sarcophan trade developments.
t.Holberg: The Feasters of Marrow were all killed at Wunderkind Fields, and the Holberg Chamber of Commerce was tagged in Faraden diplomacy.
t.Kallavesa: Heroes protected the Pilgrim's Trail from the Asaveans, though High Voice Chiara survived and vanished, and Kallavesi mystics were offered vision quests in the swamps.
t.Karov: The deadly black glass in the vale of Bulgakov was cleansed, making it habitable.
t.Liathaven: After the fighting in Bregasland, Liath's Ring gained the under threat quality.
t.Madruga: The southern reaches became a strange star-metal-infused marsh, the Children of Wrecks formed a navy and a Thunderous Deluge was unleashed across the territory.
t.Mareave: Options to address the arid climate, including Skouran aqueduct ruins, were laid out, alongside diplomacy with the Golden Pyramid, the Skourans and the Brine Turtles.
t.Miaren: The followers of the Braying Lord escaped from the Soured Pasture and their whereabouts are unknown.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Marcher experts from Mitwold were invited to help bring prosperity to Mareave.
t.Morrow: The Shuddering Wrast was killed and the rest of the Druj defeated at Iulia's Grove.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos remains annoyed at Imperial involvement in the failure of its joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Mournwold: The Miners of the Mourn were rescued, the Jotun lost their last cache and several battles, and the traitor Dalton Royse was executed by beaters.
t.Necropolis: An attempt to kill wreckers at Magazjin Plain ended in an Imperial retreat after casualties.
t.Otkodov: Diplomacy with the Thule continued, with war looming after Summer 387YE, and the situation at Shaft #3 in Nithoggir was investigated.
t.Reikos: Ghosts gathered in the shadows of High Chalcis as the Highborn year drew to a close, and volunteers were sought.
t.Sarvos: The Assembly of Ambition sought true consecration of Capodomus Cathedral, and the Grendel were all killed on the Isle of the Fox.
t.Sermersuaq: Livestock, birds and pets in Sermersuaq and neighbouring territories became inexplicably wilder.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Mareave's prosperity could attract more Imperial Orcs from distant Skarsind.
t.Spiral: Renegade former Urizen in Ankra began attacking Imperial citizens, while the Wailing Gyre was destroyed in Apulus.
t.Tassato: The Jotun were defeated at Felladonni Woods and the ilium there protected.
t.Temeschwar: The Braying Lord and its followers were slain in the Putrid Fields, at some cost in Imperial casualties.
t.The Barrens: Emperor Vesna addressed the Empire on the Barrens, the Fangs came under Senate control, a quest into the Untrod Groves was planned and a Navarr wayhouse completed in the Bleaks.
t.Therunin: Highborn and Navarr sought to lay its ghosts to rest and heal the Sephals Cauldron's taint, while Druj plans in Sweetglades and Peakedge Song were thwarted.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Upwold Seed Exchange inspired a Senate appraisal, and Upwold experts were invited to Mareave.
t.Volodmartz: The wolves of Nadezhdikov were soothed in the Choked Forest of Perumaki.

r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Druj at Bronwen's Stand were all killed.

386YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: As winter storms swept the Empire, the Brass Coast knew rare peace while the Grendel commander Gallum Fiersach still held Morajasse. Imperial armies pursued a three-fold strategy against the Jotun in the Mournwold, Urizen's shore faced a Grendel armada and Children of Wrecks pirates bent on Elos, and four armies fought the Druj in Therunin. The Gryphon's Pride marched to seize the Rahvin mithril mine in the Fangs, a crime under Imperial law, and other captains opposed them. Four battle opportunities were offered: Visten in Redoubt, Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms in Therunin, and Jarl Haakon in the Mournwold. Skirmishes at Charoko and the Iron Grove headed a long list of conjunctions.

n.Dawn: Dawn fielded a force weight of 60, its armies were barred from Cautious Advance and Give Ground, and citizen patrols forced the Druj to need 25 victory points for a beachhead in the Barrens, where several conjunctions were also offered.
n.Druj: The Druj faced four Imperial armies in tainted Therunin, were the foe in two Therunin battle opportunities, and were targeted by conjunctions in the Forest of Ulnak, the Salt Flats of Sanath and Therunin's East Ashes.
n.Grendel: The Grendel kept Gallum Fiersach in Morajasse but stood on the defensive in Ayereed and Mareave while their retreating armada struck at Redoubt, and conjunctions targeted their forces in Icarion and Maistir Varden in the Petrified Forest.
n.Highguard: Highguard contributed a force weight of 23, its High Exorcist was named for a ghostly conjunction in Reikos, and Highborn armies retained bonuses for fighting between Morrow and Zenith.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: listed with a force weight of 5 and noted as able to take the Forge Hammers order in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The Jotun faced a three-fold Imperial strategy to hold Marcher land and cut them off from their Liathaven base, with Jarl Haakon a battle opportunity and conjunctions against their yegarra and Halbera Strongarm in the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: Navarr fielded a force weight of 60 and Navarr-held lands drew conjunctions, including stopping a horde at Deer's Folly in Hercynia and rescuing a treetender in Therunin, where Imperial armies fought the Druj.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast enjoyed a rare peace across Kahraman, Madruga and Feroz, with the kamkrag deterring raiders and Wind Lord Saoirse burning Morajasse's battlements with Sand lore ahead of an assault that never came.
n.The League: The League contributed a force weight of 22, the Mayor of Caricomare was charged with saving Charoko in Sarvos from a sea beast, and conjunctions threatened Spiral's Block and Screed.
n.The Marches: Marcher land was the prize in the war against the Jotun over western hills, while Marcher armies kept their home-territory strength bonuses, could billet in Bregasland, Upwold and Mitwold, and fielded a force weight of 34.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a conjunction in the East Floes of Sermersuaq asked the Mediator of Wreck to soothe the Thule of Volham.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Redoubt shore faced the Grendel armada and Children of Wrecks pirates targeting Elos, with Visten a battle opportunity, while patrols in Morrow and Zenith forced the Druj to need 25 victory points for a beachhead.
n.Varushka: Varushka fielded a force weight of 17, kept patrols in Ossium raising the Druj beachhead threshold, could use Hospitality of the Boyars there, and was offered a conjunction to find the Chosen of Samkǒma in Brez.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark had the largest force weight at 63, kept its Fight with Honour order and special modifiers against the Jotun, and faced conjunctions in Kallavesa and Sermersuaq including the Redshal farmers' threat to the Iron Grove.

t.Madruga: Madruga was quiet and remained uncontrolled as Imperial scouts explored it and the Grendel armada withdrew, while a conjunction to the Crucible tasked Sakari Nightscale with killing mage-killers.
t.Mareave: Mareave saw no movement as the Grendel stayed on the defensive, though conjunctions sought to kill Grendel in Icarion and secure a ship's crew in Sinfoyard.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies could billet in Mitwold and the Drakes gained strength fighting there.

t.Mournwold: The Mournwold was the heart of the war over western hills against the Jotun, with Jarl Haakon a battle opportunity, the Tusks strengthened there and conjunctions in Alderly and Greensward.

About today.d: No public report followed Ambassador Kindra Surefoot's talks with Rak on extending the peace, and the Thule appear to expect a heavy price. If the treaty lapses, war follows in six months, with Thule fortifications and stockpiled mana threatening the north. Warlock Hoosfa Mek arranged for Thule skuldyr to swap non-military tales with Wintermark scops and offered a shared book of stories. The Five Fang Consortium will repay its bonds in full from its mithril mine. Two conjunctions were announced: Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn to find the missing Chosen of Samkǒma, and Halvind Brinegold to calm rogue Thule threatening Wreck's food caravans. Rak deferred talks on Suaq hunting rights until the treaty is settled.

n.Thule: The Thule hold the treaty's fate in their hands, while showing a gentler side through skuldyr storytelling and the Five Fang Consortium's full repayment of Imperial bonds. Some of their people also face trouble: the Chosen of Samkǒma are missing and a rogue band of Volham threatens trade.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Custodian of the Gift of the Dwindling Star, Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn, was asked to find the missing Chosen of Samkǒma. Void's cabalists warned that the orcs may have made a deal with Fly-the-light.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Kindra Surefoot leads the treaty talks as Ambassador to Otkodov, and Wintermark scops were invited to swap five tales with Thule skuldyr at the Moot Circle. Mediator of Wreck Halvind Brinegold was asked to calm rogue Thule.

t.Miekarova: A conjunction was announced for Miekarova to search for the Chosen of Samkǒma, who vanished after leaving the Red Lantern in Void. Combat is possible, and innocents may be present.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov's peace with the Empire runs out at the Summer Solstice 387YE, and the Thule fortifications and mana stockpiles there make war a serious threat. Hunting-rights talks wait on the treaty.
t.Sermersuaq: Rogue Thule crossed into Sermersuaq and threatened the food caravans from Wreck. Rak put off Suaq hunting rights negotiations until the peace treaty is settled.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi is not named directly; Warlock Askja, who oversees the Wreck trade, disavowed the rogue band.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz is not named on the page; its only Varushkan links are the Gift of the Dwindling Star and its Custodian.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada is the likely setting of the Miekarova conjunction to find the missing Chosen of Samkǒma, though the page names only the territory.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: Warlock Askja dropped vague hints about incidents in Urdur when suggesting the rogue Thule were under some malign influence.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: A Thule band crossed into northern East Floes and is threatening the Wreck food caravans. A combat-likely skirmish is expected there.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The rogue Thule are threatening caravans on the East Floes border with the Silver Peaks.
r.Verthandi/Askja: Mentioned in passing: only Warlock Askja appears, disavowing the rogue band and asking the Mediator of Wreck to calm them.
r.Verthandi/Hengill: Mentioned in passing: Hengill is not named on the page; it is covered only through the wider treaty situation with the Thule.

According to principle.d: The Commonwealth remained locked in war with Jarm over Lantir. Moved by Gisli Baerson's donation, Professor Gelberg's academics arrived offering him a first Beurteilung (appraisal). They proposed auctioning further appraisals from Spring 387YE, which would need a Senate motion welcoming them. Engineer Poldi Hellebrant continued building the diplomatenschloss in Necropolis, uneasy about the nearby Jarmish embassy. Commonwealth ports now offered war goods such as Soul Honey, War Amulets, Bloodclay and Hero Stone instead of herbs, ingots and measures. The Asavean bounty curtailed Commonwealth shipping. The Empire assured the Commonwealth it would not contact Viyerda. Holberg's 250th anniversary drew Commonwealth interest, and the League Assembly could issue a supportive statement of principle.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Commonwealth soldiers joke that enough Soldatentrunk on the breath could drive the orcs of the Mallum away.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the new diplomatenschloss replaces the embassy destroyed during the Grendel attack on Madruga.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Ingenieurin Hellebrant oversees the embassy's construction from quarters in the Highborn town of Hedra.
n.The Brass Coast: The Commonwealth appreciated Freeborn efforts to protect trade in the Bay of Catazar, and recalled Commonwealth soldiers fighting beside the Freeborn at the fall of Siroc. It was also kept informed about events in Madruga.
n.The League: The Commonwealth showed keen interest in Holberg's 250th anniversary. The League Assembly was offered the chance to uphold a statement of principle welcoming Commonwealth guests and endorsing Commonwealth ideals, which could lead to closer ties.
n.Urizen: The Commonwealth was reassured that the Conclave had worked with Sadogua to extend the wards protecting the Lyceum and its Commonwealth Schloss until Winter 387YE, though it wants its magicians brought home.
n.Wintermark: Gisli Baerson of Wintermark, "the Provider", received a commendation from the Commonwealth generals for donating mana and coin. He was offered the first appraisal by Professor Gelberg's scholars.

t.Bay of Catazar: Freeborn efforts to protect trade in the bay were welcomed, but the Asavean bounty kept the long journey from the Sea of Steel treacherous for Commonwealth merchants.
t.Holberg: Holberg's 250th anniversary drew interest from Commonwealth historians. Professor Gelberg's expedition planned to visit its walls, markets and university, though the Militärattache could not attend.
t.Madruga: The old Commonwealth embassy destroyed in the Grendel attack on Madruga is being replaced, and the Commonwealth was pleased to be kept informed of the situation there.
t.Necropolis: Construction of the fortified diplomatenschloss continued in Necropolis; most of the weirwood had been supplied but much white granite was still needed. Its engineer worried about Jarmish vessels sharing the Couros river.
t.Redoubt: The Lyceum and the Commonwealth Schloss on the island remain protected by Sadogua's wards until Winter 387YE, and the Commonwealth wants a way found to bring its magicians home.
t.Sarvos: The Commonwealth warship Bemühen landed Professor Gelberg's party of scholars at the Sarvos docks. They engaged a Sarvos printing house to publish their findings.

r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Poldi Hellebrant oversaw construction of the new Commonwealth embassy from her quarters in the town of Hedra.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Professor Gelberg was based at the General Benbow Inn in Cigno, where Gisli Baerson could send a winged messenger to commission the first appraisal.

All the wind.d: Mistress Karadragha offered condolences for the Asavean raid on Meade but no reparations, and declined any joint resistance to Asavea or Imperial help against dissidents. Celestial Arch visitors found the Muhnkhabat hostile to the Jotun and respectful of Asavea, the Jokhi warning that Asavea was arming Faraden extremists, and the Altantsetseg fearing Faraden could be crushed between two empires. Caitun's trade shifted towards giant blood whelks, and yak goods were offered in place of weltsilver. The Holberg Chamber of Commerce was asked to vote on an enclave including a Hall of Five Flames in Holmauer. The Gloaming Road was abrogated, and Mina i Yashum i Riqueza later funded the Parador of Wind and Flame.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as one of the nations a Faraden caravan would trade with along the Blood Red Roads to Holberg.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Muhnkhabat treated Imperial Orc visitors with polite disdain until convinced they were nothing like the Jotun.
n.Jotun: The Muhnkhabat bear a particular dislike for the Jotun, especially the Lasambrians, and fear a Jotun turn against Faraden, while Asavea dangles support for reclaiming Menendram and Talemas. Lasambrian tolls on Faraden caravans also helped end the Gloaming Road.
n.The League: Building on a statement of principle from the League National Assembly, the Faraden sought a trading enclave in Holberg, with Holberg's Chamber of Commerce to choose whether it would focus on cloth, spice, iron or nothing at all.
n.The Marches: The Marcher ambassador Ebenezer received sympathy but no reparations for the Asavean attack on Meade, and was offered yak products from Caitun rather than live yaks for the Marches.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Blue Silk Scarf guild showed interest in meeting Varushkan artisans to discuss fabrics and trade.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is named as a nation a Faraden caravan might trade with on its way along the Blood Red Roads.

t.Holberg: The Faraden proposed a Firewind Market in the upper city and a caravan enclave in the lower city, with the Chamber of Commerce due to vote on which goods the market would focus on or whether to reject it.
t.Mitwold: Faraden offered only condolences for the Asavean warships' attack on Meade, launched from a Faraden port, and accepted no responsibility. No more mithril had yet reached the Alder of Meade after the Gloaming Road ended.
t.Sea of Snow: Giant blood whelks native to the Sea of Snow, potted along the Pelabuhan coast, were to be supplied in greater number to Imperial fleets at Caitun at the cost of some orichalcum.
t.Upwold: Mistress Karadragha warned against introducing yaks to Upwold, as they are suited to high altitudes, and the civil service confirmed that past attempts had all failed expensively.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: Holfried is not named; it is linked only through the wider proposal for a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Faraden wanted land in the parkland of Holmauer for a caravan enclave that would include a Hall of Five Flames, a shrine with resident Faraden priests, which could prove a sticking point.

Bitter and absolute.d: Having raised former slaves only to serf status, the Suranni had played the Empire and the Asavean-backed Freedom Accord against each other for concessions. The Ducal Council would now befriend anyone friendly to them, though it left the door open to a stronger stance later. The Senate's Free Trade treaty and narcotics ban, meant to last three years, had boosted Suranni trade, mostly via the Brass Coast. Sarcophan vessels had become a regular presence at Robec. Separately, Suranni salvagers asked Golden Fleet Salvagemaster Caleb of the Cenotaph to clear ghosts from the sunken Singing Riqueza, a deep-water task only merrow could undertake.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Suranni count recalls a former Imperial ambassador hiring a duke's orcs to fight the Grendel, and wonders whether there were any Grendel to fight.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast merchants benefited from the rise in Suranni trade, which flowed mostly through their lands, and Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo of the Brass Coast was still serving as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy pending the Senate's Winter decision.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named on the page; the link appears to be the underwater salvage of the haunted Golden Fleet ship Singing Riqueza.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: although Feroz was described as largely back in Imperial hands, Suranni caravans still preferred to trade through Segura instead.
t.Madruga: The unnatural marshes spreading across southern Madruga frightened Suranni merchants, who called them Dumon's Sump and spread tales that they were full of infernal forces.
t.Segura: Segura became the favoured route for Suranni caravans trading with the Empire, even with Feroz largely back in Imperial hands.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat, the Tour Lavasse in Chaubrette, apparently lies to the west of Veroigne.

By northern shores.d: Around six thousand soldiers of the Gryphon's Pride, joined by fourteen Dawnish captains and one each from the Marches and Wintermark, attacked the Rahvin at the Fangs. Magistrates confirmed the order was illegal, but the Military Council's generals have full discretion. More than thirty Dawnish captains, with forces from Varushka, Navarr, the Imperial Orcs and every other nation, defended the suspicious Rahvin and covered their retreat east. The mine fell, at a cost of about 750 Dawnish dead. The Senate may now allocate it as an Imperial or Dawnish Bourse seat. The Rahvin vow to retake it this season, and will be wiped out if an Imperial army defends it.

n.Dawn: A Dawnish army and general carried out an illegal attack that took the Fangs, and its supporters face murder trials. More than thirty Dawnish captains, the largest contingent, fought their own nation's army to save the Rahvin, though the sept was most hostile to them.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named as the enemy Navarr and the Great Forest Orcs march to fight in Therunin, and as the former masters who taught the Rahvin to mine.
n.Highguard: Highborn captains defended the palisades and worked hardest, alongside the Imperial Orcs, to convince the Rahvin that their defenders were sincere.
n.Imperial Orcs: Significant Imperial Orc forces came to defend the Rahvin and led the diplomacy that persuaded the sept to accept Imperial help and survive.
n.Navarr: Isaella's Dance passed through the Barrens as guests of the Great Forest Orcs, gaining nearly a thousand Spears of the Pines for the defence of Therunin. Significant Navarr forces also harassed the Pride's flanks at the Fangs.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast captains joined the defence of the Rahvin, harrying the Gryphon's Pride's flanks with hit-and-run tactics across the broken terrain.
n.The League: League captains helped hold the palisades around the mine against the Gryphon's Pride while the Rahvin withdrew.
n.The Marches: One Marcher captain joined the Gryphon's Pride and now faces prosecution, while Hartell Household captains stood with the Rahvin on the palisades.
n.Urizen: Urizen captains harassed the flanks of the Gryphon's Pride, pinning down its reserves to cover the Rahvin.
n.Varushka: Significant Varushkan forces defended the Rahvin despite deep suspicion rooted in the memory of the Iron Helms and the Northern Eagle.
n.Wintermark: One Wintermark captain supported the Gryphon's Pride and faces prosecution, while other Winterfolk captains reinforced the palisades in the Rahvin's defence.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the battle is described as the first time since before the Empire that the people of the Bay of Catazar have fought each other on this scale.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Isaella's Dance entered the Barrens from Semmerholm.
t.The Barrens: The Fangs mithril mine passed into Imperial hands through an illegal attack, and the Rahvin retreated east vowing to retake it. The territory's other septs and Dawnish inhabitants wait uneasily for what comes next.
t.Therunin: The Gryphon's Pride abandoned the fight against the Druj here to march north, while Isaella's Dance and nearly a thousand Great Forest Orcs moved into Eastring to join the desperate defence.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Gryphon's Pride stormed the Rahvin's fortified village and took the Fangs mithril mine intact. The surviving Rahvin withdrew east along the coast, planning a counterattack this season.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: named as the region the Mallum once threatened from Houndsgate, and its Imperial citizens are among those waiting to see what happens next.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: its Imperial citizens are listed among those awaiting the outcome in the Barrens.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride turned north-west at the edge of the Saltmarsh, former home of the Vendarri, onto the Bitter Strand.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Gryphon's Pride cut straight through the forests of the Bleaks, home of the Karass and other septs, meeting neither orcs nor beasts.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: The Gryphon's Pride marched north through the region, avoiding Houndsgate, and met the garrison's messengers with stony silence. Its Imperial citizens now await what happens next.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Mentioned in passing: Isaella's Dance moved south into Eastring to join the defence of Therunin.

Construct Church of the Roads.d: Diego i Del Toro i Erigo, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the commission in Winter 386YE. The Chaplain of the Roads is a tenured position, appointed by and revocable by the Highguard National Assembly, and comes with a supply of liao. Construction required 10 white granite and 30 crowns and took three months. Asael provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and 10 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice. With the work complete, the Highborn Assembly was set to appoint the first Chaplain of the Roads at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly gained the power to appoint and revoke a new tenured liao sinecure charged with protecting the souls of travellers on Highguard's roads, with the first appointment due at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

t.Bastion: Bastion became home to the Church of the Roads, a completed commission providing liao to the Chaplain of the Roads.

r.Bastion/Woodbury: The Church of the Roads was built in Woodbury using white granite and crowns provided by Asael.

Construct Compassion Without Expectation.d: The monument was to be a restful garden celebrating Lady Eleanor Novarion's virtuous work in founding the Proffered Hand network. It required 4 white granite, 4 weirwood, 1 mithril and 27 crowns, with three months to complete. Contributions came in from many citizens over the following year, from Winter Solstice 386YE to Autumn Equinox 387YE. Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave weirwood and several crowns, Edward Watcher supplied mithril, white granite, weirwood and over two thrones, and Robin Meadowsweet, Hugh Gardener, Isolde of House Elyan, D'Eon, Fintan Nighthaven and Rhys Nighthaven also contributed. The recorded donations appear to cover the listed materials, but the page records no outcome.

n.Dawn: A garden monument was commissioned in the Dawnish territory of Weirwater to honour Lady Eleanor Novarion and the Proffered Hand network she founded. Supporters, including Isolde of House Elyan, contributed materials towards its construction.

t.Weirwater: Weirwater was chosen as the site of the "Compassion Without Expectation" garden, to be built in Applefell, with donations of granite, weirwood, mithril and money recorded through to Autumn 387YE.

r.Weirwater/Garthmoor: Applefell in Garthmoor was named as the site of the restful memorial garden to Lady Eleanor Novarion, though the page records no completion.

Construct Fortification in Peregro.d: Proposed by Morrow and seconded by Skarsind, the motion called for a citadel in Peregro and a disbursement of funds. It cost 80 white granite and 240 crowns and took twelve months to build. After the Spring Equinox 387YE it received support from the Towerjacks. Donations included small sums after the Winter Solstice from Rhys Nighthaven and others, large gifts of thrones and white granite from Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice 387YE, granite from Pontus Figures, and money from Corinthia of the Wise Citadel. The result was a fortification named Quicksilver's Flame in Peregro.

n.Druj: The citadel was raised specifically to keep watch over the parts of Therunin where the Druj hold sway, setting a new Imperial bulwark against them on the border.
n.Navarr: The fortification stands watch over the border of Therunin, a Navarr territory where the Druj and the vallorn hold sway.
n.Urizen: Morrow's senator proposed the motion, giving Urizen a new citadel, Quicksilver's Flame, guarding its border with Druj-held and vallorn-blighted Therunin.

t.Morrow: Morrow gained the fortification Quicksilver's Flame in its region of Peregro, built at the motion of its own senator.
t.Therunin: The new citadel was built to watch over Therunin's border, where the Druj and the vallorn hold sway.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro became the site of Quicksilver's Flame, a citadel built over twelve months with white granite and crowns to guard the border with Therunin.

Construct Gallery of Memories.d: Proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by Karsk, the self-funded motion called for 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns of labour, on top of standard costs, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice, Volya Vychodni Nebov provided 3 thrones, 5 crowns and the 10 wains of white granite, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a further crown. The Gallery was completed. The Varushkan National Assembly appoints the Curator of Memories with tenure, and could do so for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained a new money sinecure, the Curator of Memories, which the Varushkan National Assembly appoints with tenure, starting at the Spring Equinox 387YE. Varushkans Volya Vychodni Nebov and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov paid for its construction.

t.Ossium: Ossium's senator proposed the motion, and the territory now holds a permanent exhibition honouring the former cultures of its freed peoples.

r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The Gallery of Memories was built in Lomaa in Galath Fields from white granite, and the region now houses the exhibition and the Curator of Memories sinecure.

Construct Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyra.d: Proposed by the senator for Mareave and seconded by Reikos, the commission cost 50 mithril, 50 white granite and 60 crowns, and took six months to build. Its proposer stated that 60% was already funded. Irontide Flax supplied all 50 wains of mithril, and many citizens donated granite and money over three seasons, Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato chief among them. Once complete, the Lodge added 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season, housed and aided the order's Grandmaster, and gave the order mithril and income. It raised investment, Fundindelve output and taxes in Mareave and removed Clisearn's Uncooperative quality. The new title was first appointed at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named on the page; their only connection is that they held Mareave alongside the Imperial Orcs when the commission was passed.
n.Imperial Orcs: The commission created the Imperial Orc title Bonesetter of the Delving Market, appointed by the Tally of the Votes and first available at the Autumn Equinox 387YE. The Lodge also strengthened the Mareave lands they held through higher investment, taxes and Fundindelve output.

t.Mareave: The completed Lodge raised the investment level of mines, businesses and mana sites in Mareave by one. It also boosted the Fundindelve's production by 2 wains and the territory's taxation by 10 thrones each season.

r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn is where the Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyramid was built. Its completion removed the region's Uncooperative quality.

Construct Great Aqueduct of Eoradal.d: The commission cost 12 white granite, 4 weirwood, 4 mithril and 15 crowns, the crowns arising from the underdeveloped nature of Icarion. It carried 12 thrones upkeep and took three months to build. After the Winter Solstice several citizens donated money, including Pathfinder Gaddak, Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer, Karrak, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven. After the Spring Equinox 387YE Bloodcrow Rasp provided all the required materials. The completed aqueduct uses water bought from the Skourans of Jadefall to supply fresh water to Eoradal's main settlement and removes the region's arid quality while operational. Once Curstag's Way is also completed, Eoradal can support a large town, raising taxation by 4 thrones a season.

n.Grendel: Grendel held part of Mareave at the time, but the page does not mention Grendel or say which Mareave regions it controlled. The aqueduct was built and paid for through Imperial commission and citizens' donations.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Legion Engineer commissioned the aqueduct for Mareave, a territory the Imperial Orcs held in part. Once complete, it brought fresh water and the prospect of greater prosperity to Eoradal.

t.Mareave: Mareave gained a great aqueduct built in Clisearn that carries water bought from the Skourans of Jadefall to Eoradal. It removed that region's aridity and opened the way to a large town and higher taxes once Curstag's Way is finished.

r.Mareave/Clisearn: The Great Aqueduct of Eoradal was constructed as an edifice in Clisearn.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The aqueduct supplies fresh water to Eoradal's main settlement and removes the region's arid quality while operational. Once Curstag's Way is also completed, the region can support a large town, raising taxation by 4 thrones a season.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Mentioned in passing: Icarion's underdeveloped nature added 15 crowns to the cost of the commission.

Construct Micah's Stand.d: Proposed by Hercynia and seconded by Miaren in Winter 386YE, the motion authorised a self-funded wayhouse costing 12 wains of weirwood, 12 wains of white granite and 72 crowns, taking three months to build. Sister Micah (who was Earna) of the Navigators of Virtue provided the white granite and most of the money. Sorcha Embracing Fold supplied the weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams, Fintan Nighthaven and Rhys Nighthaven gave a crown each. Once completed, the Stand raised the Benefactor of High Chalcis to eight of each herb and added one Imperial roseweald to the Gardens of High Chalcis' great work production. It also created the title of Keeper of the Stand, first appointable at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Highguard: Highguard's territory of Reikos gained the wayhouse, and the Highborn Sister Micah of the Navigators of Virtue provided the granite and most of the money, which gave the Stand its name.
n.Navarr: Navarr senators proposed and seconded the motion, Navarr donors supplied the weirwood and coin, and the new Keeper of the Stand title is appointed by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators, first at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

t.Reikos: Micah's Stand was completed in High Chalcis, raising the Benefactor of High Chalcis to eight of each herb and adding an Imperial roseweald to the Gardens of High Chalcis' great work production.

Construct Oathwright Press.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave rather than a Senate vote, Prince Ergot di Cevia announced a sinecure to serve the printing needs of Tassatan citizens, students and leafleters and to meet the Oathwright Press's own demands. The announcement described it as producing 216 rings per season, with a tenured League position appointed by the League's senators and revocable by the General, National and Virtue Assemblies. Standard costs were 16 wains of white granite, 48 crowns and three months' work. Otmar van Holberg, Ergot di Cevia and Karrak supplied the materials and money after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, the Printmaster of Cevia became available for the League's senators to appoint for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.The League: The League gained a new national title, the Printmaster of Cevia, which its senators could appoint for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE, and which the General, National and Virtue Assemblies could revoke according to the announcement.

t.Tassato: Tassato gained a printing-press sinecure in Cevia, intended to serve the printing needs of Tassatan citizens, students and leafleters.

r.Tassato/Cascatas: The Oathwright Printing Press was built in Cascatas, at Cevia, and was completed using white granite and crowns from Otmar van Holberg, Ergot di Cevia and Karrak.

Construct Sergio's Kitchen.d: Announced in Winter 386YE by Lucrezia Corvinascura, Chair of the Wolf, the motion commissioned Sergio's Kitchen at standard cost of 10 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones 6 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. The project was organised by Red Raven Holding, styled the premier building society in the Empire. The sinecure provides coinage and is overseen by the Executive Chef of Sergio's, a tenured position held until death, resignation or revocation. Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the full cost after the Winter Solstice. With construction complete, the League's senators could appoint the Chef of Sergio's for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.The League: The League's senators gained the right to appoint the Executive Chef of Sergio's, a tenured, coin-producing position first available at the Spring Equinox 387YE, with the project funded by Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos, held by the League, became home to Sergio's Kitchen, a new sinecure completed after construction began in Winter 386YE.

r.Sarvos/Cigno: Sergio's Kitchen was built in Cigno, which now hosts the sinecure overseen by the Executive Chef of Sergio's.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Tromsa.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the senator for Hahnmark. It called for a Smugglers' Cove in Tromsa at standard cost: 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer supplied 3 thrones, 6 crowns and 10 wains of white granite. The cove was finished, and Imperial fleets can now support it in the same way that military units support spy networks.

n.Jotun: The Empire built a covert Smugglers' Cove in Tromsa while the territory was held by the Jotun, giving Imperial fleets a foothold that can be supported like a spy network.

t.Tromsa: A Smugglers' Cove was constructed in Tromsa and completed after Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer supplied the money and white granite. Imperial fleets can now support it as military units support spy networks.

Construct Timbermill and Sorting Yard.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar as Master of Rings, the great work required 40 wains of white granite, 20 wains of mithril and 180 crowns in labour, taking six months to complete. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the mithril, all the white granite and most of the money over two seasons, with a further contribution from the estate of the late Laszlo Gulyas von Temeschwar, who was honoured in the announcement. Once complete, it raised taxation from Temeschwar by ten thrones a season and increased business investment to provide two random measures each season. It created the Vardstein Vandal, who oversees a forest ministry caring for the Vale's natural resources, especially its wolves, elected first at Summer Solstice 387YE by Tally of the Votes of League business owners.

n.The League: League figures drove and paid for the project, and League business owners gained a new office, the Vardstein Vandal, to be elected each Autumn by Tally of the Votes, with the first appointment at Summer Solstice 387YE.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar gained a great work that increased its taxation by ten thrones a season and boosted business investment to provide two random measures each season.

r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: The Timbermill and Sorting Yard was built in Vardstein Vale, and the new Vardstein Vandal is charged with the prosperous use and vigilant care of the Vale's natural resources, especially its wolves.

Fake empire.d: Drawing heavily on the former salt lord Kaliact, Naomi described a Council of six salt lords, four storm lords and one wind lord. Each salt lord must control a bourse resource. She warned that the salt lords close ranks against the Empire and distrust it, and that bribing one without Senate authorisation could be treason. She identified possible openings: a Suranni-permitted spy network watching Tathar, bullying Sarcophan into cutting Grendel trade, and Asavean withdrawal if Shivaarn's head came with a grovelling apology. Possible informants included Ehsan, the Black Sand Circle, the North Mareave Trading Consortium, Gallum Fiersach and the Children of Wrecks. She also proposed a Regario Dossier office in Vorlach.

n.Druj: The Grendel make only occasional one-off deals with the Druj, whom they distrust. They likely feed the Druj intelligence on Imperial movements, and the Druj cannot know whether the Empire is at war with the Jotun unless the Grendel tell them.
n.Grendel: The appraisal laid bare the Salt Lords Council, its reliance on mithril, white granite and weirwood, and its subtle infighting. It also showed the nation's dependence on Sarcophan, Jarmish and Asavean support, which the Empire might seek to undermine.
