n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the five septs joining the Sunstorm are cited as evidence of the many orcs willing to support an expansion of the Regario Dossier.
n.Jotun: The Jotun trade a little with the Grendel and find them smug and dishonourable. They have confirmed that the Grendel pass them intelligence on Imperial military movements, apparently tailored to draw them into fighting the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn generals were named as well suited to approach the Grendel commander Gallum Fiersach. The Children of Wrecks, who claimed land in Madruga and colluded with the Asaveans against a Brass Coast lighthouse, were also discussed as possible negotiating partners.
n.The League: Kaliact sold her Spiral assets largely to League citizens and settled in Sarvos, where the Apulians and the Suranni embassy were Naomi's chief sources.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the pacifist orcs of the Mournwold joining the Marches are cited among the orcs willing to help the Empire.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel appear to have no diplomatic links with the Thule.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: much of the mithril the Council took from Spiral was traded with Urizen for weirwood, which was used to build the new Grendel navy.

t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel ambitions to dominate the Bay put them at odds with the Suranni. The Iron Confederacy nonetheless values the Grendel as a check on Imperial expansion across these waters.
t.Feroz: The Council installed Rahab as governor of Feroz hoping to distract the Empire from Spiral. Gallum Fiersach now holds out in Mora's Rock, and the Children of Wrecks have claimed land in the territory.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is listed among the lands where the Children of Wrecks have claimed territory.
t.Mareave: Lord Ehsan's Beoraidh, the Black Sand Circle and the North Mareave Trading Consortium, all based in Mareave, were identified as possible paid sources on the salt lords, wind lords and Grendel assets.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the pacifist orcs of the Mournwold joining the Marches are cited as orcs willing to support the Empire.
t.Raineach: Mentioned in passing: Raineach is listed among the lands where the Children of Wrecks have claimed territory.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named, though the page notes that Grendel mithril from Spiral was traded with Urizen for weirwood.
t.Sarvos: Kaliact settled in Sarvos, and Naomi held her discreet talks with the Suranni at the embassy there.
t.Shavronne: If the Suranni could be persuaded, Imperial agents might travel through Shavronne to establish a spy network or smugglers cove watching Tathar across the Cazar Straits. This was only a proposal.
t.Spiral: Kaliact explained that the Council always saw Spiral as a poisoned chalice: rich in mithril but made unbearable by the Black Plateau, and never realistically defensible. She has since liquidated her assets there, largely to League settlers.
t.Tathar: Tathar was identified as the target for a possible Imperial spy network or smugglers cove operated from Suranni lands across the straits, should the Iron Confederacy permit it.
t.Veroigne: Veroigne lies across the Cazar Straits from Tathar, near enough to see across. It forms part of Naomi's proposal for Suranni-permitted Imperial espionage against the Grendel.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the Cazar Straits are named as the narrow waters separating Grendel-held Tathar from Shavronne and Veroigne.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Mentioned in passing: Morajasse is not named, though the page discusses Gallum Fiersach, walled up and well supplied in Mora's Rock in Feroz.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Beoraidh, ruled by the disowned salt lord Ehsan, hosts the Black Sand Circle and the North Mareave Trading Consortium, all named as potential paid informants on the Grendel.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: The North Mareave Trading Consortium has bought land from Ehsan in Sinfoyard, from which it is building trade links that could make it a source on salt lords' assets.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Kaliact has bought a resplendent waterfront property in Cigno, where she now lives in luxury after defecting.

Figures from the past stand tall.d: Though Reikos had known peace since the last Druj holdout in Tamarbode fell in 380YE, the approach of the Winter Solstice brought far more ghosts than usual, with panicked letters flooding in from Chalcis Mount. The shades included Highborn, Druj orcs, League bravos, Urizen scholars and Navarr guides, victims of fighting in Reikos, Holberg, Therunin and Zenith, all bitter over their deaths or failures in life. The overwhelmed stewards sought help. A conjunction to the High Arboretum at 23:30 on the summit's second day, just after the Day of the Dead procession, would admit a hundred people. The civil service asked High Exorcist Alessi of the Basilisks of the Labyrinth to have the Highborn stewards lead a party from all nations to mediate with or exorcise the spirits.

n.Druj: Shades of dead orcs, mostly Druj warriors, rose among the restless dead in Reikos. The ghosts of those slain by Druj poison, flux and blood magic also bore witness to Druj cruelty.
n.Highguard: Highborn stewards of the dead in Reikos were overwhelmed by the ghosts, and the civil service asked the High Exorcist, Alessi of the Basilisks of the Labyrinth, to have the Highborn lead a party from every nation through the conjunction.
n.Navarr: Ghosts of Navarr guides appeared in Reikos crying out for aid in finding their way back to the Great Dance, alongside victims recently murdered by the Druj in Therunin.
n.The League: Ghosts of free company bravos, still in their finery, and victims of the bloody siege of Holberg were among the restless dead, and the stewards suggested League citizens might help calm them.
n.Urizen: Shades of Urizen scholars wailed over their deaths by poison or flux and their life's work cut short, and some ghosts came from those slaughtered by Druj magic in Zenith.

t.Holberg: Ghosts of those killed in the bloody siege of Holberg were drawn to Reikos for reasons no one could explain.
t.Reikos: Despite years of peace and healing, Reikos suffered a plague of restless ghosts from many Druj wars, too many for its local stewards of the dead to handle without help from across the Empire.
t.Therunin: Victims recently murdered by the Druj in Therunin appeared among the ghosts in Reikos, and some suspected the recent bloodshed there had called the dead forth.
t.Zenith: Ghosts of those slaughtered in Zenith by the bloody magics of the Druj were found among the restless dead in Reikos.

r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Panicked citizens of Chalcis Mount sent floods of letters to priests and exorcists, and a conjunction to the High Arboretum, where most of the ghosts had gathered, opened for a hundred citizens to deal with them.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Mentioned in passing: Tamarbode is recalled as where the eternal Llofir was expelled and where the last Druj holdout fell in 380YE.

Friend of mine.d: Asavean forces prepared a major assault on the northern Sumaah coast, with at least four likely targets including Zemeh. If Imperial fleets with at least 10,000 effective strength undertook Thwart the Blockade after the Winter Solstice, the assault would be repelled; otherwise a Sumaah city would burn. Some cynical voices argued that letting this happen would weaken a future rival. Through Ambassador Accalon, the Sumaah declined to help anchor the Way in Asavea but would not impede it. They sought rituals for scouting, raiding and defence, and urged the Synod to destroy the works tied to Vardas. Sumaah pilgrims would visit Holberg only if an assembly explicitly welcomed them.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: some argue that a Sumaah city's destruction would keep Asavean military might focused westward rather than on supporting the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard led the Empire's dealings with the Sumaah and was thanked with liao and a personal gift of Sevensalve. Accalon was also asked what rituals could be offered and what the proposed magicians' secondment would involve.
n.The League: Sumaah pilgrims would come to Holberg only if the League National Assembly, the Assembly of the Way or the General Assembly passed a greater-majority statement welcoming them. The Civil Service warned that League congregations preaching support for Solokha could provoke a diplomatic incident.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen and Varushka were the only nations whose ships had not answered the mandate urging captains to aid the Sumaah in the Sea of Salt.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan ships, like Urizen's, had not answered the mandate to aid the Sumaah in the Sea of Salt.
n.Wintermark: Ambassador Oxtitocszin hoped Rafe would receive a gift at the Winter Solstice for supporting the Republic. She also hoped Wintermark could spare warriors and ships to help defend the Sumaah coast.

t.Bay of Catazar: Freeborn efforts in the Bay helped keep Sumaah trade flowing despite the Asavean bounty. Some warned that the more obviously the Empire foiled Asavean vengeance, the more force Asavea might commit to the Bay.
t.Holberg: After Bernard Kleist bon Holberg's invitation to the city's 250-year celebration, which Oxtitocszin declined, Sumaah pilgrims of Pride, Ambition and Wisdom showed interest in visiting Holberg's walls and shrines. They would come after the Winter Solstice only if an assembly explicitly welcomed them, and could take offence at preaching in support of Solokha.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: a Sumaah courier was to deliver 33 doses of liao to the embassy in Necropolis.

Gifts of a green mother.d: Magistrate Nihm Farkas met the Watcher of Fragrant Leaves after Archmage Ibiss Briarheart's missive. The Green Mother offered several boons. One was aid in uniting the vallornhearts, if a coven cast Hallow of the Green World and let her children roam the Empire. Another was a Black Oak bough to lift the Wither the Seed curse from Brocéliande through Thunderous Tread of the Trees. She also offered milksap brewed with Churning Cauldron of Bravash, chaotic donahorti from farms, forests and mana sites, and empowered enchantments for briars and orcs. Magistrates warned they would prosecute anyone who accepted. The Silent Bell, the Senate and Netweaver's Eye were all offered as ways to detect lawbreakers.

n.Dawn: Astolat, Semmerholm and the Barrens were among the territories where the Black Oak bough could be used. Whichever was chosen would be ravaged by awakened trees so that the curse on Brocéliande could be lifted.
n.Druj: Yaw'nagrah is said to offer patronage to the Druj, but she is losing patience with their refusal to free the vallorn of Béantal Dol. She promised to help the Navarr do so instead if the Brocéliande curse were removed with her aid.
n.Highguard: Reikos and Casinea were offered as possible targets for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, and would suffer rampaging trees if chosen.
n.Navarr: The offer opened a perilous route to freeing Brocéliande from Wither the Seed, but at the risk of rousing its vallorn. It also held out the eternal's help in freeing the vallorn of Béantal Dol, alongside the Navarr's own expedition there. The herald blamed Navarr 'jealousy' for the gulf between Imperial magicians and the Green Mother.
n.Urizen: Yaw'nagrah offered to warp the Urizen rituals Fountain's Bounty and Woven Strands of Life on mana sites, producing milksap and donahorti instead of the usual yield. This relied on the complicity of Urizeni magicians and would be a crime while she remains under enmity.

t.Astolat: Astolat was one of five territories on which the bough-empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees could be laid. It would face ravaging trees if chosen.
t.Brocéliande: Brocéliande was offered a way to remove the Wither the Seed curse with the help of Yaw'nagrah's servants. Doing so would inevitably rouse its vallorn, which the Broch could only partly blunt.
t.Casinea: Casinea was listed as a possible target for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, which would bring rampaging trees there.
t.Reikos: Reikos was listed as a possible target for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, which would bring rampaging trees there.
t.Sarangrave: If the Brocéliande curse were lifted with her bough, Yaw'nagrah would send servants to Sarangrave to help the Navarr free the vallorn of Béantal Dol.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm was one of the territories on which the bough-empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees could be cast, which would leave it ravaged by awakened trees.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens was offered as a possible target for the empowered Thunderous Tread of the Trees, which would bring rampaging trees there.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Yaw'nagrah was first placed under enmity after her agents tried to rouse the vallorn of Therunin.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell risked being lost to the vallorn if the curse were removed with the Black Oak bough, and Imperial heroes would be needed to defend its steadings.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael risked falling to a roused vallorn if the Green Mother's boon were used to lift the curse, depending on which way the vallorn went.

Golden light.d: Capodomus, an ancient centre of study for the Way looted during the Grendel sack of Sarvos, had been restored after a three-year League effort. If the General Assembly sent a named priest with true liao to consecrate the Atrium of Golden Light to Ambition, the cathedral would become the pre-eminent place to study the Way. The Archbishop would gain ten extra crowns each season and could deliver an inaugural sermon heard across the Empire. Further options would include a 50-crown Lucati Gallery of paragons and exemplars, and a 30-crown tomb for Empress Giselle. Citizens could freely switch to their nation's voting resource, priests could encourage pilgrimage, and each national assembly could reward one ambitious citizen.

n.Dawn: If the consecration went ahead, Dawnish citizens could switch their personal resource to a military unit in the same territory without paying the usual fee, and their national assembly could reward an ambitious citizen each season for a year.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: as the raiders who sacked Sarvos, looted the cathedral's art and gold filigree, and carried off Empress Giselle's remains.
n.Highguard: Highborn citizens could freely gain a congregation, the resource that counts in their Tally of the Votes, and the cathedral was described as larger even than Highguard's Basilica of Seven Doors.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orcs could freely switch to a military unit, though only units supporting Imperial armies accrue votes, and Thrace, founder of the Imperial Orc nation, was proposed for the Lucati Gallery.
n.Navarr: The famous painting of the Navarr Thorn Isaella hangs in the cathedral and the guardian Thorn was proposed for the Lucati Gallery, while Navarr citizens could freely acquire herb gardens if the consecration went ahead.
n.The League: The League would gain the Empire's most prestigious seminary of the Way, a richer and more influential Archbishop of Capodomus, and the chance to bring Empress Giselle home to Sarvos, while its citizens could freely acquire businesses.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens could freely switch their personal resource to a mana site in the same territory if the mandate passed, and their national assembly could reward an ambitious citizen.
n.Varushka: Varushkans could freely switch to a mine or forest in the same territory if the consecration went ahead, and Ratibor of Temeschwar was proposed for depiction in the Lucati Gallery.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark citizens could freely switch to a military unit in the same territory if the mandate passed, and their national assembly could reward an ambitious citizen each season.

t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle refused her place in the Necropolis on her deathbed, asking to be buried in Caricomare instead.
t.Sarvos: Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos would host the true consecration, drawing pilgrims and scholars from across the known world, and could receive the Lucati Gallery and Empress Giselle's tomb.
t.Temeschwar: Empress Giselle's recovered remains rest in a modest tomb in Temeschwar that recent events made untenable, and the Archbishop could have them moved to Sarvos with little effect on Virtue's Respite.

Hammers and boxes.d: Invited by the Archmage of Autumn through Ashborn Trosk, the Architects of Iron and Stone assessed Pakaanan's Pass. The House of Fire and Flame offered to clear it for 250 measures of beggar's lye and mineral rights, if the Conclave passed a declaration before Summer 387YE. Baas Sterner of the Coalition of Stone and Struggle offered 100 crowns of labour on Curstag's Way if League business owners admitted their Strugglers, granite and mithril for ambergelt or orichalcum, and greater prosperity if the Senate relinquished the Brilliant Shore to the Imperial Orcs. The City of Gold and Lead reordered box handling, offered auctioned Broker's Box sigils and an oversized box, and sought to buy Bound by Common Cause.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the late Archmage Maurice de Gauvain died fighting unliving horrors invading Dawn, and one offered item, the Marching Banner, was made by the Dawnish weaver Yvelle Silver-Eyes.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Mareave, then held by Grendel, is named only briefly before being corrected to Spiral.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were offered help clearing Pakaanan's Pass and completing Curstag's Way. If the Senate relinquished the Brilliant Shore to them, the Coalition proposed raising its output and lifting every Imperial Orc's income by 2 rings a season for at least a year.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun, aided by the heralds of Adamant, were responsible for the damage that blocked Pakaanan's Pass.
n.The League: League business owners were to vote at a public meeting on whether to let Coalition Strugglers talk to their workers in exchange for 100 crowns of labour on Curstag's Way, despite civil service warnings about rising construction costs. The Crimson Reapers' camp was to host a negotiation over Bound by Common Cause.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are said to have kept the Imperial copy of the Immaculate Architect ritual, one of the items offered for Bound by Common Cause.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Herminius of Urizen was asked to run the Broker's Box auction in return for an oversized box, and Urizeni magicians appear in the story working on Spiral's roads.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the clearing of Pakaanan's Pass is described as potentially of interest to Wintermark, and heralds examined the pass from Sermersuaq.

t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Mareave is named once alongside Skarsind as a place the heralds came to help, before the page corrects this to Spiral.
t.Sermersuaq: Heralds of the Architects of Iron and Stone appeared in Sermersuaq as well as Skarsind while examining the damage to Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was the focus of two proposals: clearing Pakaanan's Pass, and handing the Brilliant Shore white granite quarry to the Imperial Orcs. The second would raise output from 26 to 30 wains a season and the territory's taxation by 5 thrones a season.
t.Spiral: With 38 wains of white granite, 14 wains of mithril and 205 crowns of labour still needed on Curstag's Way in southern Spiral, the Coalition offered labour and materials. Workers there were described as lacking protection from the plateau's oppressive atmosphere.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Denize, one of the roadbuilders in the story, is from Temeschwar.

r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Architects of Iron and Stone found the pass extensively blocked by mountains closed around it. The House of Fire and Flame offered to clear a route wide enough for an army for 250 measures of beggar's lye and mineral rights, an offer open until Summer 387YE.

Hard to find.d: More than three thousand questing knights, guided by the Karass, explored the Untrod Groves. They gathered dragonbone and gloaming, but a Forge the Wooden Fastness enchantment favoured the Earl, implying an older claim to the land. They reached the Earl's Dawnish-style manse before being driven back. Some yeofolk stung by the manticore became its vassals. These vassals courted minor Dawnish houses and moved towards bandits threatening the Golden Sun's baggage train. A Witch of the Silver Woods offered the Knight-Protectors an alliance against the Earl on Silverbrow's behalf. The Last Battle wayhouse opened supply routes into Sarangrave and Therunin, sheltered survivors of the Therunin rout, and awaited a Keeper.

n.Dawn: Dawnish questing knights suffered heavy losses and some yeofolk became the Earl's vassals, while several minor Barrens houses allied with the Earl. The Knight-Protectors were invited to an audience offering alliance against it.
n.Druj: The Karass, used to Druj rule, warned that the Last Battle wayhouse would hasten the Druj's return. Its supply routes now threaten Druj-held regions in Sarangrave and Therunin.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Navarr travelling through Karass lands said they got a friendlier reception from the Jotun.
n.Navarr: The Last Battle wayhouse gave Navarr a base in the Bleaks, a free new personal resource there this season and Therunin voting rights for those resources. Its Keeper, appointed by Navarr generals, faces Karass resentment.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the page compares the Earl to a hylje, which cannot truly be a member of Wintermark.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Earl's manse with banners and a tournament square was likened to a field in Astolat.
t.Sarangrave: The Last Battle established supply routes from the Bleaks into the Turan Flats and Nesustak Forest, putting those Druj-held regions under threat.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens saw the failed Untrod Groves expedition, the emergence of the Earl's vassals among Dawnish houses and the Golden Sun's camp, and the completion of the Navarr wayhouse amid Karass anger.
t.Therunin: Survivors of the bloody rout in Therunin sheltered at the Last Battle, whose supply routes now threaten Eastring. Navarr resources in the Barrens count as being in Therunin for elections.

r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Last Battle's supply routes reached into the Nesustak Forest, leaving it under threat.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The Turan Flats came under threat as the Last Battle established supply routes into them.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Unarmed vassals of the Earl visited small Dawnish settlements here, and a few houses agreed to ally with the Earl.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Earl's vassals watched events in the Fangs from Hope's Rest and courted local minor Dawnish houses, winning some as allies.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Navarr completed the Last Battle wayhouse here, angering the resident Karass, and it now shelters Therunin survivors. Well-equipped bandits threatened the Golden Sun's baggage train while the Earl's vassals moved to intercept them.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: Mentioned in passing: the Karass had asked for the Plains of Teeth to be ceded to them, and the Dawnish refused.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: A huge questing expedition was driven back by a Wooden Fastness enchantment and the manticore-like Earl of the Groves, who claims the Groves and turned stung yeofolk into vassals.
r.Therunin/Eastring: The Last Battle established supply routes into Eastring, which is now under threat.

I am easy to find.d: In Winter 386YE Emperor Vesna delivered a personal message, carried across the Empire and beyond by the civil service, concerning the orders issued to the Gryphon's Pride in the Barrens. Vesna declared that the Rahvin were foreigners protected by Imperial law, seeking to work with the Empire through legal means, and that both the Empire and Vesna had sworn no harm would come to them. Archavion was accused of hiding his scheme, waiting until Vesna could not intervene, undermining negotiations by the Earl's council, and betraying the Empire, his soldiers and his nation. Vesna branded him a criminal with no place at Dawn's hearth and vowed the crime would be answered to the fullest extent of the law.

n.Dawn: Dawn's own Emperor publicly disowned a Dawnish general, declaring that Archavion did not act in the nation's name, had brought it death and shame, and had undermined the Earl's council's efforts to secure Dawn's resources lawfully.

t.The Barrens: The address concerned the Gryphon's Pride's actions in the Barrens against the Rahvin, whom Vesna said had been under Imperial protection, leaving what Vesna called a desert that Dawn must now learn to live in.

Improve the Great Chain of Sarvos.d: The upgrade carried a special costing of 100 white granite, 300 crowns in labour and one year to complete. Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the bulk of the resources, delivering 25 wains of white granite and money after each season from Winter Solstice 386YE to Autumn Equinox 387YE, which covered the full 100 wains of granite. Smaller donations of money came from Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, Rebecca Fabbro di Sarvos, Rhys Nighthaven, Alvaro Nocciola Di Tassato, Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg, Karrak and Farren Silver Streams. Once complete, the Great Chain was upgraded to a rank two fortification.

n.The League: The League's defences in its city of Sarvos were strengthened, with Sarvos citizens among those who helped pay for the upgrade.

t.Sarvos: The Great Chain in Sarvos was upgraded to a rank two fortification once the year-long work was complete.

It never happened.d: Shuttered Lantern cabals investigated the politics of five citadels, reporting at the Winter Solstice. Ilarch Maxatios distanced Kantor from Theodosia's Peace auras. Grand Ilarch Adonai of Ipotavo collapsed after their heir Phoeb died in Imperial care, and the pro-Empire General Dancia Terricos is expected to succeed them; she invited League generals to send plans regarding the Mallum. Sarcophan investment is reopening Issyk's docks. If the General Assembly passes a mandate and 40 congregations support Solokha, the worst hauntings will be cleansed and relations improved, though supporting priests may be offered dedication to Anarchy, Vengeance or Peace. Vigilance mandates could instead study the Axou sects or watch participating priests.

n.Druj: General Dancia Terricos, a veteran of Ipotavo's defence against the Druj and the campaign that freed Kaban from the Mallum, offered to consider what part Ipotavo might play in League generals' plans regarding the Mallum.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grand Ilarch Andronicus of Issyk is said to consider the attempted Axou alliance with the Grendel a mistake.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Ambassador to Axos, Fintan Nighthaven, is of Navarr.
n.The League: General Dancia Terricos felt kinship with Holberg and asked League generals, especially the general of the Towerjacks, to send her their plans regarding the Mallum by Winged Messenger before the Spring Equinox.
n.Urizen: Axou tradition blames the Empire, and in-character the Urizen, for Solokha's fall, and Urizeni congregations cannot join any of the Solokha mandates unless they pass with a greater majority.
n.Varushka: Varushkan congregations cannot take part in the Solokha project unless the relevant mandate passes with a greater majority; a Varushkan icewalker of the Shuttered Lantern features as a spy in Axos.

t.Holberg: General Dancia Terricos, herself a survivor of a Druj siege, admired Holberg's resistance and had hoped to attend the 250th anniversary of the city joining the League, but her plans fell through.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Axos once tried to invade Spiral in retaliation for the fall of Solokha.

Lit up.d: The Golden Pyramid dropped its modest lodge plan and proposed rebuilding the green keep in Clisearn as a grand lodge. The Imperial Orcs' inspiration of Thrace could cut its cost to 50 white granite, 50 mithril and 60 crowns, and it would create a Bonesetter of the Delving Market. Using the new turtle-protection law as their pretext, the Illarawm found the Brine Turtles hostile but identified their true leader, Opaugh 'the Hook', with whom the Empire might negotiate. The Twelfth Mercenaries of Jadefall offered to garrison a Mareave citadel. Urizen historians learned of the artefact rod Stormcaller and the Courath of Icarion, leading to a conjunction against a Grendel paymaster. The Senator for Mareave was asked to save Lord Ehsan's ship, the Salt Shaker.

n.Grendel: A Grendel paymaster, accompanied by Asaveans, is expected in Icarion to pay local mercenaries to attack Imperial Orc holdings, and the Minister of Historical Research is tasked with killing him. Meanwhile the Brine Turtles still await the Salt Lords' promised but undefined return.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation could co-fund the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge through the inspiration of Thrace and gain a new Bonesetter of the Delving Market. Its Illarawm envoys have opened a cautious path to negotiate with the Brine Turtles, and Skouran mercenaries have offered it a citadel garrison.
n.Urizen: Invited by the Imperial Orc Assembly, Urizeni historians uncovered the lost rod Stormcaller of the Army of the Citadels and its link to the Courath of Icarion. This gives Urizen a stake in the conjunction against the Grendel paymaster.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: the armies of the Salt Lords could cross the border into Mareave from Ayereed at any moment.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Senate's law protecting turtles in the bay gave the Illarawm their pretext to visit the Brine Turtles and opened a small window for trust; the Salt Lords are said to have abandoned Mareave to seek riches across the bay.
t.Mareave: The territory was offered a transformative grand lodge, a possible treaty with the Brine Turtles and a Skouran citadel garrison. Two conjunctions also arose on its soil and coast.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel's unsuccessful invasion of Redoubt is cited as a sign of Mareave's exposure.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Lord Ehsan's independent Beoraidh continues to seek closer trade ties and has adopted Imperial currency. Its representative warned of the Grendel paymaster, and Ehsan asked the Senator for Mareave to rescue his ship, the Salt Shaker, promising a small gift in return.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: The Golden Pyramid proposed rebuilding Clisearn's green keep, with Ehsan's old villa, into a grand lodge that would boost the Fundindelve and local investment. It would also remove the region's Uncooperative quality by ending the open opposition of the local families.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Skourans have offered aid in rebuilding Eoradal's aqueduct. Locals there gave Urizeni historians only one-word answers about the Courath.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Illarawm spent the season in Fioroult and found the Brine Turtles guarded and loyal to the Grendel. They identified the fisherman Opaugh 'the Hook' as the town's true leader, whom the Empire could approach by winged messenger.
r.Mareave/Icarion: A Grendel paymaster is due to meet local mercenaries led by the Courath of Icarion, the last reputed holder of Stormcaller. This creates a highly likely combat conjunction there.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Mentioned in passing: Nadir is not named on the page and is covered only as part of Mareave's general situation.

Little faith.d: The Great Library of Hacynian, where the Empire found the way to defeat the vallorn, was becoming a pilgrimage site for Navarr, grey pilgrims and historians. Three mandates were proposed: one directing scholars to research chosen topics (vates, Empress Giselle's death, the volodny), one having visiting magicians codify a ritual, and one embracing Night Singer and Phaleron, the eternals linked to the Library's regio. The General Assembly upheld Judgement 34, the third option, so Nathair Autumngale consecrated the Library, and an administrative motion was raised to create the title Singer of the Silence, appointable from Spring 387YE. Separately, the Navarr could commission a Vinery whose Keeper would receive herbs and a Bloodcloak; that opportunity has since expired.

n.Navarr: The Navarr were the people most affected, as the prospect of defeating the vallorn within their own lifetimes spread a fierce urgency through the nation and drew more healers to the oaths of the vine. The nation was offered a chance, now expired, to build a Vinery whose Keeper, appointed by the National Assembly, would receive herbs each season and a Bloodcloak each year.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League are noted as applying their ingenuity to the problems arising from the Library's revelations about the vallorn.

t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is the location of the Great Library of Hacynian, but the page does not name the territory or describe any effect specific to it.

Made anew.d: Captains taking Explore the Southern Reaches mapped Siroc Bayou, the Crucible and the Quiet Grasses, which remain uncontrolled. The Unfettered Mind traced the marsh's strange flora, fauna and temporary regio to Spring, Night and Winter magic, Azoth, Ossegrahn and diffuse ilium. The Rod and Shield found Grendel camps and confirmed that the Children of Wrecks' navy, the Gathered Storm, lies at Free Landing. They also found that armies cannot cross to Feroz or Segura now the bridges are gone. Grendel and Asavean mage-killers in the Crucible were left for Sakari Nightscale to face. Opportunities included marsh flowers, the Rainbow Conservatory, Sand Crab Camp, the Chimes of Silence and the Enigmatic Tower college.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: many Dawnish captains are listed among those who explored the southern reaches.
n.Grendel: Grendel encampments were found and neutralised in the marshes, and an abandoned Grendel supply camp became Sand Crab Camp. A large band of Grendel and Asavean mage-killers still lurks in the Crucible, readying a last raid on the Rod and Shield.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: one Highborn captain, Thomas, is listed among the explorers.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the only link is that the new southern marshes are contrasted with those of Bregasland.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: several Navarr captains are listed among those who explored the southern reaches.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn captains led the exploration of their transformed territory, and many of the opportunities discovered would benefit the Brass Coast, including a possible Mistress Sand Crab title and a Freeborn-only venture. Bakar i Riqueza funded the Parador of Salt and Sand expansion, while the Gathered Storm's stolen Storm Child figurehead taunts the Freeborn.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League ingenuity helped Rod and Shield magicians reach the Enigmatic Tower, and a League writer is evoked in the opening tale.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher, Billiam, features in the opening tale, John a Woode is listed among the explorers, and Marcher landskeepers might be drawn to the proposed Enigmatic Tower college.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen explorers are listed, a conversation with an Urizen magician helped inspire the Chimes of Silence, and the proposed tower college might attract Urizen stargazers.
n.Varushka: The Rod and Shield proposed that Lutomysla Niegoslava bring Varushkan road builders south to appraise how a durable road could cross the Night-and-Spring infused marshes. Several Varushkan captains also took part in the exploration.
n.Wintermark: Sakari Nightscale, Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield and a Kallavesi mystic, is responsible for dealing with the mage-killers in the Crucible and would receive the order's oddities if they are killed. Many Wintermark captains joined the exploration, and Wintermark mystics might be drawn to the proposed tower college.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Children of Wrecks' new navy, the Gathered Storm, can now threaten any settlement along the Bay of Catazar, alarming the people of Quzar and Calvos.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are contrasted with the warm new marshes of Madruga, and a Bregas mage features in the opening tale.
t.Feroz: The Midpoint bridge is destroyed, so Imperial armies still cannot move between Madruga and Feroz. The Rod and Shield suggested a Varushkan appraisal to find a way to build a lasting connection.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are contrasted with the warm new marshes of southern Madruga.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the ilium particles infusing the Scorrero and the new marshes were swept down from Kahraman's mountains.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are contrasted with the warm new marshes of southern Madruga.
t.Madruga: The territory's southern reaches have been remapped as three uncontrolled, transformed regions full of altered creatures, shifting land and temporary regio. Opportunities there include marsh-flower herb gardens, the Rainbow Conservatory, Sand Crab Camp, the Chimes of Silence great work and the Enigmatic Tower college, and the Parador of Salt and Sand has been expanded to trade in Adversity vis.
t.Ossium: The Drownbark Forest shares the ilium-infused waters and Night magic of the new marshes, and an appraisal might find a way to grow marsh flowers there.
t.Raineach: Mentioned in passing: rumour holds that the Temple of Tempest Jade there is one of the bastions helping to sustain the Children of Wrecks' navy.
t.Segura: The Cerevado bridge is gone, so armies cannot move between Segura and Madruga until a new crossing is built. Altered creatures from the marshes have been sighted as far upstream as Cerevado.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Children of Wrecks' control of the Cazar Straits is one of the holdings that lets them sustain their new navy.
r.Madruga/Crucible: The Crucible is now an uncontrolled, wild and enigmatic marsh where Grendel and Asavean mage-killers lurk and a powerful sense of boundless possibility grips visitors. It holds Sand Crab Camp and the Enigmatic Tower, and is a possible site for the Rainbow Conservatory.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Children of Wrecks have completed their navy, the Gathered Storm, and anchored it at Free Landing, its flagship bearing the stolen Storm Child figurehead.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: The former Great Grasses are now the uncontrolled Quiet Grasses, home to strange tall trees and a profound silence. Cabella i Riqueza has proposed the Chimes of Silence great work there, and hakima explorations of the region inspired the Parador expansion.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: The former Siroc Plains are now the Siroc Bayou, a wild, uncontrolled and hallucinatory marsh of mangroves and altered beasts. It is a possible site for the Rainbow Conservatory.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Its existing mix of ilium-infused marshwater and Night magic makes it the likeliest place outside Madruga where an appraisal might allow marsh flowers to be cultivated.

Million miles of water.d: For Eoradal, Skourans from Jadefall offered to supply water through a restored Great Aqueduct for 12 thrones a season, or in exchange for exclusive mining rights in Eoradal, Clisearn and Nadir. They also offered a Healer's Pool. A former Grendel mage, Ila Bared, instead proposed secretly tapping a Skouran lake via the Yellow Fish Adit. For Nadir, the Senate could buy Marcher cattle for a Southern Herd, or an archmage could seek help from Kimus or Ossegrahn. For Icarion, the Freeborn could build a qanat, or the River Doubt in Apstrus could be dammed. Doing both would make Icarion an oasis. Several options lapse after Summer Solstice 387YE.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Ila Bared, who proposes the Adit scheme, is a former Grendel magician-merchant, and the page recalls three Grendel armies broken at Solen's Doubt.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orcs faced choices over how to make Mareave's arid regions liveable, from a Southern Herd with a Shepherd sinecure to a Healer's Pool with an elected Bonesetter. Their Assembly could also send a sept to help the Freeborn in Feroz or Madruga in return for the Freeborn's aid.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun are not named, but farmers from Bregasland, which they held, are listed among those who could drive cattle to Wayford.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn experts, some of whom designed Segura's Iron Qanat, offered to build an Icarion Qanat for little more than token payment. In return, the Imperial Orcs could send a sept to help rebuild Feroz or Madruga.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League's Assembly is named among those that might object to flooding the Fallen Valley, where many who died freeing Spiral are buried.
n.The Marches: Marcher experts from Mitwold and Upwold judged Mareave's land poor. Marcher farmers could be offered cattle-bonds to sell their herds to the Imperial Orcs at the Spring Equinox, and Marcher military units could help escort the drovers south.
n.Urizen: A Urizeni visitor, Severina, proposed damming the River Doubt at the abandoned spire of Solen's Doubt to water Icarion. The Urizeni Assembly is named among those that might object to flooding the Fallen Valley.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka's Assembly is listed among those that might object to flooding the Fallen Valley, where many fallen heroes lie.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the arid eastern shore of the Bay and the bitter winds blowing in from it are described.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland farmers are named among those who could drive cattle to the Wayford market.
t.Feroz: The Imperial Orc Assembly could mandate a sept to travel to Feroz to help the Freeborn rebuild, instead of exploring Mareave.
t.Madruga: An Imperial Orc sept could be mandated to go to Madruga to help the Freeborn rebuild, repaying the aid given in Mareave.
t.Mareave: Mareave was offered several ways to end the aridity of Eoradal, Nadir and Icarion, including an aqueduct, a cattle herd, a qanat and a dam. Each brought costs, possible tax gains and new political complications with Skoura.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold sent Marcher experts to Mareave, and its Wayford cattle market could gain holding pens for cattle bought under the bond scheme.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold's mining is referenced in the opening story, and its farmers could drive cattle to Stockland.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's Iron Qanat is cited as the model for the proposed Icarion Qanat.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's Great Herd is the model for the proposed Southern Herd, and orcs there might be drawn to settle Mareave.
t.Spiral: The River Doubt in Spiral could be dammed to divert water to Icarion. This would require Towerjacks or a Bound by Common Cause army to work under the Black Plateau's deadly influence, and would flood a mass grave.
t.Upwold: Upwold sent Marcher experts to Mareave, and its Stockland cattle market could take in cattle for sale to the Imperial Orcs under the bond scheme.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: the lights of Beoraidh are glimpsed in the distance in the opening story.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn's eastern hills could be handed to Skouran miners as exclusive mining rights in exchange for water.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal could have the Great Aqueduct restored with Skouran water or water tapped secretly through the Yellow Fish Adit, ending its aridity and, once Curstag's Way is complete, supporting a large town. A Healer's Pool could add further taxation.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Icarion could lose its arid quality through a Freeborn qanat or a dam on the Doubt. With both, it would become an oasis adding 6 thrones a season.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Nadir's aridity could be ended by driving a Marcher-bought Southern Herd there or by eternal aid in reaching deep reservoirs, though drakes would threaten the cattle. Its hills could also be given to Skouran miners.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Mentioned in passing: Icarion's mining camps send their ores to the town of Aghnayadh in Sinfoyard.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The River Doubt near Solen's Doubt in Apstrus is the proposed site for a dam and reservoir to feed Icarion. This would flood the Fallen Valley, resting place of thousands from eight Imperial armies.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Mentioned in passing: Apulus's hills run into Icarion, but the region is too low to supply water economically.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the dam work would take place in a troubled site outside Screed itself.

Mistaken for strangers.d: The Kulsdottir trading house sought invitations to games of chance, and heralds of the Commander in Crimson and Gold came to the Wintermark camp. They offered Blaze Dunning's circle a dialogue, three draughts of a changeling-making liquor to unlineaged contestants judged by High Bard Tarik, and boons for captains who fought beside the Knights of Glory. The Stzena of Tears, leading freed husks north after the Deadwood Knight's fall, sought Dawn and Varushka. Others included the Falconer's diplomats, the Azoth's herald hiring musicians, two Ketsov facing inquisition, Seventh Wave unconquered, merchants from the League and Spiral, and Marracossan exiles. After five Synod judgements, a small Sand Fisher group planned to arrive on the final day.

n.Dawn: The Stzena of Tears, seen leading leftover husks out of Wickmoor, sought Dawnish representatives, and the Falconer's envoys asked to meet a senator in Dawn's glory square. A community supporting Laroc was divided over yeofolk who had left to seek glory.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns fought the Druj in Therunin, and the Sand Fishers are described as former Druj slaves.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard fought the Grendel in Redoubt, the Marracossans recalled defending Trajadoz against the Grendel invasion, and a League merchant sought investors for a trade mission with the North Mareave Trade Consortium.
n.Highguard: A Highborn priest of Prosperity from Reikos came to sell Isazaiya's incense to fund research into Tamarbode's mushrooms. Highborn unconquered of the Seventh Wave invited Anvil's unconquered through a conjunction to their Mournwold camp.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Falconer's two envoys asked to meet a senator in the Imperial Orc fighting pit at 21:00. Generals of the Granite Pillar and Tusks could each nominate a captain to receive a boon from the Lion of Summer's herald Rikkan.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes, Granite Pillar and Tusks fought the Jotun in the Mournwold, and the Seventh Wave's scouts were on the front lines against them.
n.Navarr: The Urizen questor Varinius extended his dreaming opportunity to Navarr dedicants of Wisdom he had met before, and the Black Thorns' general could nominate a captain for Rikkan's boon. The High Roller came to Anvil at the invitation of the Navarr vate The Red Bramble.
n.The League: The League camp expected merchant Dieter D'Apulian seeking investors and, on the final day, the Sand Fishers answering the League Assembly's invitation. Rahuun Amahuz of Spiral returned, and the Marracossan exiles of Trajadoz came to thank the Artisan's Guild.
n.The Marches: The Drakes, who fought the Jotun in the Mournwold beside the Knights of Glory, could nominate a captain for a boon. The Seventh Wave's unconquered opened a conjunction from their camp at West Millston after helping secure Imperial victory in the Marches.
n.Urizen: Varinius, a questor from Eudokia's Spire, offered twelve places for dreaming to Urizen and Navarr Wisdom dedicants he knew, gathering at the Hub because the Urizen tea rooms might be closed. The Citadel Guard's general could nominate a captain for Rikkan's boon.
n.Varushka: The Howling Queen's Stzena of Tears, leading husks north into Varushka, came to discuss the Deadwood Knight's fall and her relationship with Varushka. Two Ketsov from Ossium came to have their kin's Virtue held to account in an inquisition.
n.Wintermark: The Kalpaheim trading house the Kulsdottir sent a representative to settle obligations from the Chocolate Game and seek invitations. Heralds of Eleonaris held their contests in the Wintermark camp, with Scarrow Dawnbreak nominated to greet and escort them.

t.Astolat: A small community supporting Laroc lost several prominent yeofolk to the pursuit of glory, with Helene Fletcher urging their return and Jean Cooper defending their choice.
t.Holberg: The Sand Fishers, living richly in Holberg's marshes and keen not to jeopardise their new lives, nervously agreed to send a small group to Anvil to learn what the Empire wanted of them.
t.Mareave: League merchant Dieter D'Apulian sought investors for a potential trade mission with the North Mareave Trade Consortium, presented as an opportunity rather than an agreed deal.
t.Mournwold: Imperial armies fought the Jotun here alongside the Knights of Glory, and with fighting still ongoing, the Seventh Wave's unconquered opened a conjunction for six visitors to West Millston in the Chalk Downs.
t.Ossium: Two Ketsov, from the Ossian settlement of that name, travelled to Anvil seeking an inquisition into their kin's Virtue, in an encounter involving themes of cannibalism, slavery and violence.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard fought the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks in Redoubt beside the Knights of Glory, making its general eligible to nominate a captain.
t.Reikos: A Highborn priest of Prosperity from Reikos brought three doses of Isazaiya's incense and one experimental dose to sell, raising funds for her research.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Marracossan travellers passed through Sarvos, and Dolce and Novella di Sarvos authored two of the Sand Fisher judgements.
t.Spiral: Rahuun Amahuz returned to Anvil to build on the Circle of Black Sand's ambition to become an up-and-coming power in Spiral, seeking progress and further introductions.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns fought the Druj in Therunin alongside the Knights of Glory, making their general eligible to nominate a captain.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Synod praised the Sand Fishers for making a home in Misericorde, discovering and guarding the Flaxen Pillars and repaying a loan for its sawmills, while the Prince of the Misericorde Market invited them to Anvil.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Mentioned in passing: the Rebeshof Roadwarden was among those inviting the Sand Fishers to Anvil, and had written to Swift Fisher.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: The sale of Isazaiya's incense at Anvil was meant to fund her ongoing research into the mushrooms of Tamarbode.

Obsidian shards.d: Just as Spiral seemed to be stabilising, a caravan bringing arms from Holberg to the Ballaghadruh garrison was massacred, and the Prismatic Garden was overrun and looted. A dead attacker's obsidian shard symbol was identified by Caela of the Silver Flame as belonging to the Spire of Black Glass, former Citadel Guard sentinels turned conspiratorial under the Black Plateau's influence. Caela and other former rebel leaders disavowed them. Leaguish and Urizen folk worked together and learned the sentinels meant to damage the Block and kill researchers in Screed. Magistrates deputised over a hundred citizens. The Senator for Spiral, Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, was charged with defending the Block, and the Oblivion Sentinel, Floria Sunshaper, with protecting the researchers, both in fights to the death under the Plateau's malign influence.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: lingering questions about contact with the Grendel are noted, and the Spire of Black Glass's origins are traced to the battle of Solen's Doubt against them in 382YE.
n.The League: Leaguish interests were among those targeted, beginning with the massacre of the Holberg arms caravan, and Leaguish citizens worked alongside Urizen to uncover the sentinels' plans.
n.Urizen: A Urizen spire was wiped out by renegade sentinels from among the former rebels, whom Caela of the Silver Flame disavowed, and the Oblivion Sentinel Floria Sunshaper was charged with bringing them to justice.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the slaughtered caravan was carrying weapons and armour from the forges of Holberg.
t.Spiral: Spiral's fragile peace was shattered by murders and looting from the Spire of Black Glass, whose sentinels threatened the Block that restrains the Black Plateau and researchers sheltering there.

r.Spiral/Ankra: The Holberg caravan was found slaughtered in a pass on the edge of Ankra and Ossuary, and the Spire of Black Glass's abandoned citadel lies on Ankra's border.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Former rebels' status as foreigners relies on the Senate recognising their control of Cinion, and a free company scouting a pass there spotted the armed sentinels on the move.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The massacred caravan was discovered in a pass on the edge of Ossuary and Ankra, near the abandoned Spire of Black Glass on Ossuary's border.
r.Spiral/Screed: Researchers studying the Black Plateau in Screed were caught out of position and faced massacre unless the Oblivion Sentinel's forces stopped the sentinels hunting them.

On southern sands.d: Urizen magicians laid storms, healing waters, Summer citadels and Autumn enchantments across Redoubt. The Citadel Guard, Towerjacks and Northern Eagle then prepared its defence. A Grendel armada raided the coast and made a full assault on Elos, which was driven back. A second, chaotic attack by the Children of Wrecks followed, including former Freeborn, League and Marcher fighters, and it too was repulsed. The defenders of the Lighthouse at Nikephoros collapsed it into the sea rather than let it fall. Redoubt stayed under Imperial control, and the Towerjacks left temporary fortifications in Naris. Further wreckers raided the interior, which set up a solstice battle opportunity to protect the Ribbon of Salt and Visten.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe is named among the armies that invaded Ayereed in an earlier season, in the background to the Ayereed conjunction.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their poisoning of the Lower Tarn Valley cost the Northern Eagle nearly two hundred soldiers, and the Children of Wrecks' savagery is compared to theirs.
n.Grendel: Their Broken Shore armada raided Redoubt and threw its full strength at Elos, but was forced to retreat without a foothold and lost ships to the storms and to Children of Wrecks pursuers. Separately, a Grendel maistir was sent to fund mercenaries to retake the Imperial foothold in Ayereed.
n.Highguard: Necropolis would have been threatened had Elos fallen. The Highborn traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is among the turncoats to be slain at Visten Head, and if he escapes the wreckers could plunder Highguard lands.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven, which they hold, is named only as the home of the lost striding that the traitor Ioan Bloodstride came from.
n.Navarr: The armies sent to Redoubt marched out of war-torn Therunin. The Navarr traitor Ioan Bloodstride, who joined Siakha's forces at Meade, is a target at Visten Head; if he escapes, the wreckers could raid Navarr lands.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel force included ships that assaulted Madruga and burned Siroc, and ex-Freeborn fought among the Children of Wrecks and the wreckers who raided the Spire of the Wealdawn.
n.The League: The Towerjacks fortified the Redoubt coast and Elos Harbour, held the docks against both assaults and left temporary fortifications across Naris. League traitors fought among the raiders, and the Uccelini Maurizia Spada di Sarvos is a target at Visten Head.
n.The Marches: Perhaps half a dozen Marcher warbands, their livery removed, fought with the Children of Wrecks at Elos. This soured hopes that the recent conflict with the Marches had been laid to rest.
n.Urizen: Redoubt was defended by the Citadel Guard and Urizen magic, and the Assembly's warning helped prepare its people. Elos was damaged, the Lighthouse at Nikephoros was destroyed and the Littilian Fast was sacked, but the territory remains fully under Imperial control.

t.Ayereed: The Lord of Gainmeachdubh sent Maistir Varden with funds to pay mercenaries to retake the Empire's foothold and destroy the new smugglers' cove. The Imperial Spymaster, Bernard Dugdale, is charged with killing him and may free an unknown captive in his company.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel armada came at Redoubt from the open sea, raising fears that it had crossed the heart of the Bay. Both the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks retreated into its deep waters, fighting each other as they went.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' fortification work is credited to Holbergian ingenuity.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the traitor Ioan Bloodstride is described as a refugee from a lost striding in Liathaven.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel force that attacked Redoubt included ships and soldiers that had earlier assaulted Madruga.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Ayereed is described as the territory to the south of Mareave.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: not named; the only Marcher link is the disguised Marcher warbands at Elos, who were thought to intend returning to the Marches.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard marched south out of Morrow, and the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle passed through it by Highwatch on their way to Redoubt.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel beachhead at Elos would have threatened Necropolis as well as Redoubt.
t.Redoubt: Wrapped in Imperial curses, healing waters and magical fortifications, Redoubt saw off the Grendel and the Children of Wrecks and remains fully under Imperial control. It suffered casualties, storm damage, reduced fleet and ministry income and odd effects on farms, herb gardens and forests.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: lingering ill-feeling over Spiral is noted, as is Redoubt's readiness for attack from that direction.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle left war-torn Therunin to reinforce Redoubt.

r.Ayereed/Gainmeachdubh: Its Grendel lord sent Maistir Varden, with a guard of Grendel and Asaveans, to pay mercenaries to retake the Imperial foothold in Ayereed.
r.Ayereed/Petrified Forest: The Empire's foothold and newly begun smugglers' cove here are the target of the mercenaries Maistir Varden has been sent to hire.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the earlier Grendel assault on Madruga.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is one of five turncoats to be killed at Visten Head.
r.Redoubt/Limus: A cohort of Autumn constructs led by minotaurs strengthened the garrison of Cargo, whose walls burned with sigils binding them to Shikal. The Spring storms reached even here.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Naris bore the Grendel landings and both battles of Elos, and the Lighthouse at Nikephoros was destroyed. The Towerjacks left a temporary fortification here that fades by the end of Summer 387YE.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: Autumn constructs reinforced the Court of the White Fountain, to the unease of its koboldi. Later, wreckers who had sacked the Littilian Fast headed into Optarion.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: A Summer citadel of pale stone and dark ice, garrisoned by bear-like heralds, rose on Mount Siluri, and the Citadel Guard marched south through the region to the coast.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: The Northern Eagle defeated Black Eels raiding the Brilliant Star. Wreckers later landed in southern Tomari and sacked the Littilian Fast.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Mentioned in passing: the Spring storms were felt as far north as Willstone.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Northern Eagle lost nearly two hundred soldiers marching through this Druj-poisoned vale, the only route that would get them to Redoubt in time.

One of us.d: Missionaries, helped by Freeborn smugglers, kept heading east after the Synod vetoed a Senate ban on preaching in Asavea. The project to establish the Way there needs 750 wains of white granite and 280 thrones, but only 37 thrones, 2 crowns, 1 ring and 1 wain had been given. The Sevenfold Path contacted three groups: the Cerularios, who want the shield Glistering; the death-obsessed Mikanos covenant, who want ten doses of true liao; and the rebellious magicians of Becephelas, who want Imperial lore. Winning each over would lower the cost. The Loyalty assembly could back violent rebellion against the Plenum or slow reform from within. The Whisper Gallery taunted that one group is a Plenum double-agent.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: only indirectly, as the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion is used to measure the vast amount of white granite needed for Asavea.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: as a warning, the Lasambrians are recalled as having marched off to fight alongside the Jotun after the Empire brought them to Virtue.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the white granite needed to establish the Way in Asavea is likened to the amount used to build the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion.

Over western hills.d: Ten Jotun armies besieged Landskeeper's Bulwark in Freemoor, where the Tusks and the Granite Pillar held on, and King Gudmundr offered terms of surrender. Marcher and Imperial Orc armies then struck through Alderly into Southmoor, while Highborn, Wintermark and League armies advanced from the south. In the Battle of the Oakleaves, rebel Mournfolk opened Sarcombe's gates to the Tusks and the Bounders. Threatened with losing their supply lines, the Jotun withdrew into Liathaven. Six thousand Imperial soldiers fell. Chalkdowns, Ore Hills and Greensward remain Jotun-held, and the Senate may now assign the territory. Knights of Eleonaris fought on both sides. A battle opportunity was offered to kill Haakon.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Highborn Assembly statement cites the Druj being forced back and the septs they enslave as further targets of the crusade of Loyalty.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Highborn armies left the fronts at Feroz and distant Ayereed to fight in the Mournwold.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar helped hold Landskeeper's Bulwark, and the Valiant Pegasus and the Seventh Wave (sped by Autumn magic) joined the southern push on Sarcombe. The Highborn Assembly's crusade of Loyalty gives anointed Highborn an extra hit point in the Mourn, and two competing mandates are proposed: one to hold conquered Jotun regions, one to strike into Hordalant.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm and the Autumn Hammers marched with the Marcher armies through Alderly into Southmoor, part of the northern strike that helped break the Jotun hold.
n.Jotun: Despite their overwhelming numbers, the Jotun lost Southmoor and Sarcombe and withdrew into Liathaven to protect their supply lines, paying a heavier price than the Empire. Jarl Haakon defied King Gudmundr and Queen Yrsa to hold Farstrider's Watch with many champions, and still keeps Chalkdowns, Ore Hills and Greensward.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr armies were part of the alliance pushed out of the Mournwold before the Autumn Equinox, and Miaren is named as a likely line of retreat from Freemoor.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the southern Imperial force came up into Southmoor from the Brass Coast, where the Jotun had expected an attack from Kahraman.
n.The League: The Wolves of War joined the southern advance on Sarcombe, backed by independent captains and battle dancers of the Shadowed Flame. A Sarvosian consortium has offered to buy Haakon's effects for a museum if he is slain.
n.The Marches: The Tusks held Landskeeper's Bulwark and, with the Bounders, took Sarcombe when Marcher rebels opened its gates. Mournwold is Imperial again and likely, though not certainly, to be assigned to the Marches. The Strong Reeds guarded Bregasland, and Marchers who supported the Tusks or the Reeds may gain extra endurance through anointing.
n.Wintermark: The Narwhal's Spear raided the Jotun, linked the separate Imperial forces and helped rebels in Ore Hills and Chalkdowns. A yegarra champion, Halbera Strongarm, has since challenged their general, Determination of Ice Kaisa.

t.Ayereed: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave came from the distant Ayereed front, sped to the Mournwold by Autumn magic.
t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds stayed to defend Bregasland, turning back Jotun champions who tried to push into the marshes from Graven Rock and earning the grudging respect of the locals.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar marched from Casinea to reinforce Landskeeper's Bulwark.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus marched north from Feroz to join the attack on Southmoor.
t.Hordalant: A proposed alternative Highborn mandate would strengthen Highborn armies attacking into Hordalant. It competes with a mandate to hold conquered Jotun regions.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had expected an Imperial attack to come from Kahraman.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun armies retreated west into Liathaven after the Empire threatened the supply lines that run out of it into Southmoor.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as a place the Freemoor defenders might be forced back into.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher and Imperial Orc armies set out through Mitwold, where the Drakes had earlier repelled ships on the river Meade.
t.Mournwold: The Empire won Southmoor and with it control of the territory, which the Senate may now assign. Jarl Haakon still holds three regions from Farstrider's Watch, and the Jotun have not given up their ambition to retake it.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn are said to look west towards the wealth along the coast of the Sea of Snow.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named as a possible line of retreat for the Freemoor defenders and as a direction the Jotun expected an attack from.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Jotun and their Summer allies still hold the fortified Graven Rock, but the Strong Reeds' vigil kept them pinned there and unable to turn on the Imperial forces.
r.Hordalant/Vallorberg: Mentioned in passing: the yegarra Einar the Cunning came from the forests of Vallorberg to raid Alderly.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The northern Imperial force advanced through Alderly into Southmoor, and a later Jotun strike to cut supply lines there was foiled by the Narwhal's Spear and the Drakes. Bryce the Hare must now stop Einar's yegarra hunting a New Longstwick herbalist.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Chalkdowns remains under Jotun control, but rebellion grew there as Jotun armies tried to stamp out the guerrillas.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The Jotun swept into Freemoor and besieged Landskeeper's Bulwark, but the Tusks and the Granite Pillar held it, refused Gudmundr's surrender terms and repelled a later assault by the Fell Hammers and the Mandowla's Roar.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: a third of the Jotun forces turned towards Alderly and Green March, and the northern Imperial force passed through woods on its border.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Jarl Haakon now holds the region from Farstrider's Watch with veteran warbands and champions. A battle opportunity to kill him was offered, with Friar Heggy Rosemund of the Greensward joining the fight.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Still Jotun-held, Ore Hills was a centre of rebellion: Imperial heroes aided its miners, defeated three Summerborn champions, and the miners armed resisters elsewhere.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor was conquered by the Empire after victory at Miller's Crossing and the Battle of the Oakleaves, when rebels opened Sarcombe's gates. The town was scarred by the fighting and Jotun control there was ended.

Patterns of fairytales.d: The Silver Chalice aided flood victims in Segura and Kahraman, saving hundreds of lives, and wealthy Freeborn offered to plan a Chalice grand lodge on the Coast if endowed with 25 crystal mana. The Penumbral Veil altered most Imperial night skies. A Wyrm–Mountain conjunction left older war-enchanting arcane projections unusable but exchangeable for mana. The Church of The Little Mother took over the Loom of Spells and will auction it. The Mystics of Ishal named three possible Meeting Place sites, and the Sentinel Gate will open to their Aviary. Sadogua's heralds joined Marcher Wassails, and Azoth, Lashonar, Barien, Basileia's heralds and an unknown herald announced visits to Anvil. A thousand Bleak Knights remain camped in Madruga.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the herald from the Silver Woods says her sister has business with Dawn this summit, and expects Wintermark to keep nosy Dawnish away from her own meeting.
n.Grendel: Gentle rains in Grendel-held Feroz help wash away scars of Governor Rahab's occupation, Feroz is named as a suitable site for a Silver Chalice lodge, and developments in Mareave had halted earlier lodge plans.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the night skies above Highguard's Casinea are, for some unexplained reason, untouched by the Penumbral Veil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: orcs in Skarsind are among those in the north-west who may have suffered unsettling animal attacks.
n.Jotun: The Silver Woods herald walked out of Jotun lands, Jotun-held Tromsa, Skallahn, Hordalant and Bregasland border all three candidate Meeting Place sites, and the City of Locks has accepted a contract on the life of Jarl Haakon in the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the skies above Therunin are untouched by the Penumbral Veil, and Hercynia is among the north-western territories seeing more animal attacks.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn suffered over two hundred flood deaths and widespread homelessness, eased by Silver Chalice relief; Segura's bridges and the Cerevado Nets are broken, the Sunset Roads stay closed, and Bleak Knights loom over Quzar in Madruga.
n.The League: Tassato's gossips mourn the loss of Sanvar Isk as the Church of The Little Mother takes over the Loom of Spells and its mountebank work crews, and plans to auction access to it.
n.The Marches: Sadogua's heralds joined Marcher Wassails, Blessing of New Spring farms not using Yaw'nagrah's boon will yield Shinemoon elixirs, a Well of Shadows door appeared in Tower March, and Upwold enjoyed gentle rains.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Ematius of Urizen, as Archmage of Winter, declined Tharim's new deal, and the Urizen ritual Quick Study is noted as working with the Loom of Spells.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's servant the Almighty Panjandrum will continue to answer Missives for Sadogua sent by Varushkan magicians.
n.Wintermark: The Mark gains Sadogua's full backing for Dripping Echoes of the Fen on Rundahl Marsh, a Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Aviary of Ishal, praise for the mystic Wiglaf, Sorin's cold prosperity in Hahnmark, and visits from Barien's herald Timbrel and the Silver Woods herald.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as an Imperial territory its night skies fall under the Empire-wide Penumbral Veil.
t.Bregasland: Coracle Rock, an ancient dolmen on the border of North Fens and Hordalant's Blutgahn, is one of three possible sites for a new Wintermark Meeting Place.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's night skies are inexplicably untouched by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Feroz: Gentle rains help wash away the scars of Governor Rahab's occupation, and Feroz is named as a suitable location for a Silver Chalice grand lodge.
t.Hahnmark: Wintermark magicians brought cold prosperity to herb gardens as Sorin's servants culled weak plants, and the territory is among those seeing more animal attacks.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is listed among north-western territories where people may have had unsettling encounters with animals.
t.Hordalant: Coracle Rock, on the border between Blutgahn and Bregasland's North Fens, is a candidate site for the new Meeting Place.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman suffered some flood damage and receives Silver Chalice relief until Summer 387YE; Gambit is now the only secure route into the Sobral, though Kahraman is thought a poor choice for a lodge.
t.Kallavesa: Dripping Echoes of the Fen cast on Rundahl Marsh will now protect the whole territory, the Sentinel Gate will open to the Aviary of Ishal, and Gull's Isle on its border is a candidate Meeting Place site.
t.Madruga: Madruga's blight prompted the flooding, Segura cannot now be reached from it, its skies escape the Penumbral Veil, and a thousand Bleak Knights camp in Lightsea while some wander to watch people.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: developments in Mareave halted the Chalice's lodge plans, and the Golden Pyramid's proposed structure there is the yardstick for any Coast lodge.
t.Mournwold: Its skies are spared the Penumbral Veil, Night heralds joined Wassail even here, and the City of Locks' Guild of Accountants is working on a contract to kill Jarl Haakon here.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as an Imperial territory it lies under the Empire-wide Penumbral Veil.
t.Segura: Segura bore the brunt of the flood: two of three bridges are destroyed, Cerevado's waterfront flattened, the Cerevado Nets damaged and the Sunset Roads closed, though Silver Chalice aid saved many lives and it is a candidate lodge site.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq sees a rise in attacks by mundane animals and restless guardians, borders Gull's Isle, and received a mysterious herald at the garrison of Rest in Stark.
t.Skallahn: Gull's Isle, a tidal island in the Gullet on the border of Skallahn, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, is a candidate site for the new Meeting Place.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among north-western territories where unsettling animal encounters may be roleplayed.
t.Tassato: Tassato's salons lament Sanvar Isk's fall while the Church of The Little Mother's child overseers now drive the Loom's mountebank crews, though they pay actual money.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the night skies above Therunin remain untouched by the Penumbral Veil.
t.Tromsa: The shores of Lake Nutjuitoq, where Tromsa meets the Suaq Wastes, are one of three potential sites for a new Meeting Place.
t.Upwold: Gentle rains fall on Upwold, a Well of Shadows door appears in Tower March, and the Tharim herald Obligatus remains at the Copse of the Bone Birch while two companions are unaccounted for.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Coracle Rock on the North Fens border is a candidate site for the new Meeting Place.
r.Hordalant/Blutgahn: Coracle Rock, on Blutgahn's border with the North Fens, is one of the Mystics of Ishal's three candidate sites.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: With the bridges down, Gambit is now the only secure way to enter the Sobral and Segura from the north.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: A Sentinel Gate conjunction will open to the Aviary of Ishal in Skymark at 22:05 on Friday for a Goosewhisper ceremony.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: A thousand Ashen Knights loyal to Tharim remain camped in Lightsea near Quzar, showing no sign of leaving.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Sobral Bridge is the only crossing left standing, leaving the Sobral reachable securely only via Gambit.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The garrison of Rest in Stark was visited by the Witch or Wit of the Silver Woods, an unidentified herald seeking ambitious icewalker diplomats.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The shores of Lake Nutjuitoq where the Suaq Wastes meet Tromsa are a candidate site for a new Meeting Place.
r.Upwold/Tower March: A round green door to Sadogua's Well of Shadows appeared in an ancient oak a day's hike east of King's Stoke, reached by a newly remembered path.

Pride and paragons.d: Gaelen Embercast's judgement, passed by a greater majority, confirmed that Vardas was a fiction written by Ivar Olyankavic Nathavolava. This prevented a schism, and people did not start doubting the other paragons. Instead they questioned where the signs of the paragons come from, what exemplars are for, and why a paragon may embody only one Virtue. Grieving archivists agreed to stay at the Lepidean Library only if it avoids researching paragons and exemplars for a year. They offered to research one of the three questions for the Librarian instead. Their delayed work on Tom Drake prompted an informal appeal to the Marcher Assembly. Donations to the Grand Inspiration have slowed sharply, which threatens a decade's delay.

n.Dawn: Dawn's national assembly had encouraged donations to the Grand Inspiration, but those contributions have now stopped. Highguard has invited Dawnish priests to preach in Bastion, yet some Highborn worry the troubadours may preach glory and love rather than the Virtues.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Highborn preacher's sermon claims Imperial generals have dragged the Druj to the verge of destruction.
n.Highguard: Highborn faith has been shaken by Vardas and the Assembly of Nine's troubles: donations to the Grand Inspiration have fallen to about ten wains a season. Many traditional Highborn archivists at the Lepidean Library are grieving and threatening to retire.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs declined to support the Grand Inspiration and chose to build a Library of Worth instead.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr was among the nations that donated to the Grand Inspiration, and the Highborn Assembly invited it to send priests to Bastion; its donations have since ended.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen rejected the call to support the Grand Inspiration in favour of its own projects, though its Assembly stopped short of calling it folly.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka declined to support the Grand Inspiration and created its own Hall of Fabric Arts instead.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark was among the nations that donated to the Grand Inspiration and were invited to send priests to Bastion; its donations have since stopped.

t.Bastion: Construction of the Grand Inspiration in Bastion has 583 of 1000 wains of white granite and 167 of 250 thrones. With donations waning it could take a decade to finish, and Highborn doubt is growing over what will be preached there.

Raise Third League Army.d: Passed in Winter 386YE, the motion carried the standard costs of 200 mithril and 75 thrones, with twelve months to complete. Donations arrived over the following year from many individuals, including several Holberg and Tassato names. By far the largest contributor was Vesna Borkovna Prochnost, who supplied most of the mithril and thrones in several instalments, including 105 wains of mithril and 55 thrones after the Winter Solstice 387YE. Once complete, the new army, the Sparrows Reckoning, finished mustering shortly before the Summer Solstice 388YE. It was engaged in Bregasland over the following season.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page notes only that the new army was engaged in Bregasland, which the Jotun held when the motion passed.
n.The League: The League gained a third army, the Sparrows Reckoning, raised in Tassato and paid for by donations from many citizens, several of them from Tassato and Holberg.

t.Bregasland: The newly mustered Sparrows Reckoning was engaged in Bregasland in the season after it finished mustering before the Summer Solstice 388YE.
t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the Sparrows Reckoning was raised in the territory, with a number of Tassato citizens donating mithril and money towards it.

Raise Third Varushkan Army.d: The motion called for the third army of Varushka to be 'reborn from losses on the Eastern front'. It was proposed by Karsk, seconded by Karov, and passed. The commission carried standard costs of 200 mithril and 75 thrones and took twelve months to complete.
