After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Blazh Zbignev provided the 200 wains of mithril and almost all of the coin, 74 thrones 4 crowns 2 rings. Radic Splinterovich Schaslyvyy, Kostjya and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave the remaining small sums. With the work complete, the new army, the Boyar's Hasta, was raised in Karov.

n.Varushka: Varushka regained a third army, the Boyar's Hasta, replacing forces lost on the Eastern front. Its own senators proposed the motion and Varushkan citizens such as Blazh Zbignev paid almost all of the cost.

t.Karov: Karov's senator seconded the motion, and the Boyar's Hasta was raised in the territory once the twelve-month commission was complete.

Redesign Pallas Docks.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Segura, the motion acted on the Autumn proposal of the Debruin Family of the House of the Bear, set out in the Hyenas and herbs wind of fortune. The renamed Debruin Docks would stay an Imperial Bourse position, overseen by the Prime Factor of the Pallas Docks, to bolster the Senate's funding. The Ambassador to the Delves supported it. The project was to be self-funded, costing 90 crowns and taking three months. After the Winter Solstice, Marta Kotova Novikova gave 11 thrones and 1 crown and Kostjya gave 1 crown. Once complete, the Custodian of the Pallas Docks becomes the Custodian of the Debruin Docks.

n.Urizen: The redesigned ministry sits in Urizen-held Redoubt, where an unused set of docks is to be revived as a trading post for weirwood from the Sarcophan Delves.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt's long-unused Pallas Docks are to be rebuilt and reopened as the Debruin Docks, an Imperial Bourse position for buying weirwood from the Sarcophan Delves.

r.Redoubt/Limus: Limus is home to the Pallas Docks, which the motion renames the Debruin Docks and redesigns for the weirwood trade once three months of work are complete.

Reestablish Herds of Afar.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by the senator for Kahraman. It commissioned work, as outlined by the civil service, to reestablish the herds of Afar and to create a new sinecure, the Dhomiro of Afar. The commission cost 300 crowns, took three months to complete, and was to be entirely self-funded. After the Winter Solstice 386YE, Garviel i Abrira i Erigo contributed 37 thrones and 2 crowns, and Karrak and Farren Silver Streams each gave 1 crown. With the work complete, the Dhomiro of Afar was to be appointed for the first time at the Spring Equinox 387YE by Tally of the Votes of Freeborn fleet owners.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is linked only because it held part of Feroz that season.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a new title, the Dhomiro of Afar, to be chosen by their fleet owners, and saw the herds of Afar restored in Feroz.

t.Feroz: The senator for Feroz proposed the commission, which restored the herds of Afar and created a sinecure to oversee them in the territory.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Afarjasse became home to the restored herds of Afar and the seat of the new Dhomiro of Afar sinecure.

Remodel Virtue's Rest.d: Proposed by Reikos and seconded by Spiral, the motion commissioned the remodelling of the great work Virtue's Rest as detailed in the War of Thorns and Flowers wind of fortune. The work cost 120 crowns plus the usual costs of the opportunity, and took three months. Cyrus of Ebon's Hall, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven contributed towards it. The remodelling completely removed the investment and returns Virtue's Rest had previously offered. Instead, eligible armies of Navarr, Highguard, Varushka and the League could take the Resupply in Virtue's Rest order in Bastion to improve their resupply. The new Exarch of Virtue's Rest would first be appointed at Summer Solstice 387YE by the votes of Highborn congregation owners.

n.Highguard: Highborn citizens gave up the hostels they had offered to pilgrims so they could shelter recovering soldiers, and Highguard's armies can now resupply at Virtue's Rest. The new Exarch of Virtue's Rest is chosen annually by Highborn congregation owners.
n.Navarr: Navarr armies are among those eligible to take the Resupply in Virtue's Rest order in Bastion, which improves their resupply during the War of Thorns and Flowers.
n.Varushka: Varushkan armies are among those eligible to resupply at the remodelled Virtue's Rest in Bastion, which strengthens their recovery during the war.

t.Bastion: Virtue's Rest in Bastion was rebuilt from pilgrim hostels into a recovery place for soldiers. It lost its former investment returns but now offers the Resupply in Virtue's Rest order to eligible armies.

Rumblings in the Gullet.d: A week before the Winter Solstice, a brief quake struck along the Gullet, causing minimal casualties and only partial collapses of a few older buildings in neighbouring territories. Strange stonework, coral and body parts then washed ashore, investigators vanished, and long-dead husks were seen capsizing fishing boats and pulling people under. Westerhal fisherwoman Ingrid Longsight disappeared. The husks were judged no military threat but a matter for heroes. Around a dozen threatened Reed's Roost in the North Fens, under Haylock Blackthorn's responsibility; another dozen harassed Westerhal, with Kjellen Saltmire asked to act; and injured survivors stranded on a sand bar in Stark were entrusted to Nekoda, who might learn the threat's source from them.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held territories of Hordalant and Skallahn felt a small impact from the quake, and the husks are likened to a Jotun warband in scale.
n.The Marches: Reed's Roost in Marcher Bregasland faced a band of around a dozen husks, with its Reeve, Haylock Blackthorn, charged with stopping them before they damaged the building and reduced its mana crystal output.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark bore much of the threat: Westerhal's fisherfolk in Kallavesa faced husk attacks and the loss of Ingrid Longsight, while injured survivors stranded off Sermersuaq were placed in the care of Nekoda, Claviger of the Basilica of Cora Holdfast.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland felt the quake, and beaters from Greywater tracked a dozen husks heading for Reed's Roost, due to arrive a few days after the Winter Solstice.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is listed among the neighbouring territories that felt a small impact from the quake.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa felt the quake and saw fishing boats capsized and crews dragged under, with Westerhal's fisherfolk threatening to withdraw inland unless Kjellen Saltmire defeated the husks.
t.Sermersuaq: A missing fishing boat's survivors were reported stranded and in great pain on a sand bar off Sermersuaq's coast, and Nekoda was made responsible for tending them.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Skallahn is listed among the neighbouring territories that felt a small impact from the quake.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Reed's Roost in the North Fens was threatened by around a dozen husks; its folk prepared to leave, and failure to defeat the husks risked damage to the Roost and lower mana crystal production.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The fishing settlement of Westerhal in the West Marsh was harassed by a dozen husks, risking damage to the fleet and reduced voyage production if they were not stopped.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Wilda, a host of Sulkavaris, reported survivors stranded on a sand bar in Stark, whose treatment might reveal the source of the husks and how to counter them.

Second star.d: Captains who chose riches came home weathered but wealthy, each bearing one star-bright gem; any vessel enchanted with Golden Voyage may now join that option. Those sailing deosil to mystery were led on whimsical fetch quests and must continue one more season to reach unknown seas and gain a map. Those sailing straight on for glory were driven by unceasing winds but suffered grievous attacks from Asaveans, Grendel pirates and unknown foes, and must persist two more seasons; personal Summer enchantments are encouraged. Six buyers, including a Thule Dragon, Azoth, a Varushkan boyar and the Prince of the Argent Tontine, are offering to purchase the gems through Ephisis Boxes, but only this season.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel pirates are named among the enemies that attacked ships sailing straight on for glory.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Tathenon the Gyre, one of the Thule Dragons, has offered to buy all the Empire's Fire Rubies for an unknown purpose.

t.Sea of Snow: Captains turning widdershins by riches were harassed by krakens in the Sea of Snow on their perilous voyage home.

Secret meeting.d: Meraud's herald Ethod warned that the Golden Magician was trapped and failing, and asked for the return of items he had made, including Urizen's Churnspire regalia and two rings. Sorin agreed to a strictly conditioned parley and offered an appraisal of one fortification or army for 160 drams of true vervain. Yaw'nagrah declined to parley but offered illegal boons. Estavus's heralds proposed clearing Pakaanan's Pass and finishing Curstag's Way. Zakalwe identified a chance to confront Jarl Haakon at the Sentinel Gate and offered gifts to Marcher generals and mana sites. The Whisper Gallery invited artworks containing secrets. The Prefects offered a Declaration of Concord on publishing plenipotentiaries.

n.Dawn: The heralds arrived at Dawn's Castle of Thorns, and Meraud's messenger could only come thanks to the Golden Magician's Fayre laid across Dawn by Phoenix Rising. The Summer Archmage, Mirella of the Twisted Rose, was to meet his apprentice.
n.Druj: Yaw'nagrah's herald said the Druj she escorted to Brocéliande were fleeing slaughter in the Barrens, and that she prefers some Druj to many Imperials because they reject the shackles of civilisation.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: a young magister at the Castle of Thorns was described as fresh from the seminary at Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Archmage of Day Gralka received Zakalwe's response, and Architects of Iron and Stone assayed the Jotun damage to Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind, bringing an offer from the House of Fire and Flame to clear it.
n.Jotun: Zakalwe's emissaries studied Jotun strategy in the Mournwold and identified a chance for Imperial heroes to confront Jarl Haakon outside Farstrider's Watch, using the Sentinel Gate. Their earlier damage to Pakaanan's Pass was assessed for repair.
n.Navarr: Yaw'nagrah refused to escort the Navarr into Brocéliande, saying the children of Terunael can do that themselves, though she was interested in the claim that the Empire would connect the vallornhearts.
n.The League: A herald of the Coalition of Stone and Struggle studied Curstag's Way in southern Spiral, then presented proposals at the Palace in Apulian for finishing the road, along with requests that might have wider implications for the League.
n.The Marches: Zakalwe praised Marcher generals, especially Amberlain and Stanley, for putting their people's defence first, and offered personal gifts to all four generals. He also offered Marcher mana sites transformed by Carve the Crystal Guardian two pawns of prismatic ink.
n.Urizen: Urizen held three archmagecies. Meraud asked for the return of the Staff of the Storms and Mask of the Geyser, part of the Churnspire Adjutor's regalia, to help free himself from the snare that binds him.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's parley would ask the former Dawnish coven of Whelps whether they wish to bring the Empty One's power to Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Archmage of Night Eliina Lailasdottir was granted a meeting by the Whisper Gallery, and assayers of the Architects of Iron and Stone explored the mountains of Sermersuaq around Pakaanan's Pass.

t.Astolat: The heralds of the eternals came to the Castle of Thorns to deliver their responses, including Ethod with a Skyborn guard and Sorin's bone-masked herald Ossium.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe said the magical fortification at Graven Rock offered no opportunity like the one found against Jarl Haakon.
t.Brocéliande: Yaw'nagrah explained that the Druj she brought here were refugees and refused to escort the Navarr in. She offered illegal boons tied to the Empire's plan to connect the vallornhearts and wake the forest's trees.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is not named on the page; at most it is touched by the parley question of bringing the Empty One's power to Varushka.
t.Mournwold: Zakalwe's emissaries assessed the Jotun here and identified a chance to confront Jarl Haakon via the Sentinel Gate, with a report going to the military council. They noted that the people of the Mourn are heartened when generals keep their promises.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the novice magister at the Castle of Thorns had recently come from the seminary at Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only as that of Sorin's herald, Ossium, who delivered the Empty Throne's response.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is not named on the page and has no direct connection to the events described.
t.Sermersuaq: Assayers of the Architects of Iron and Stone explored the mountains between Sermersuaq and Skarsind, assessing how Pakaanan's Pass might be repaired and reopened.
t.Skarsind: Autumn assayers examined the Jotun damage to Pakaanan's Pass, and the House of Fire and Flame offered to clear it with explosive tools, as set out in Hammers and boxes.
t.Spiral: A herald of Shikal's Coalition of Stone and Struggle studied the coast and the work on Curstag's Way in southern Spiral, talking only with the labourers, before offering proposals to complete the road.

r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: Terunael appears only in references to the Navarr as 'children of Terunael' and to the 'great work of the Terunael' of connecting the vallornhearts.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Assayers evaluated the damage the Jotun did to the pass and how it might be reopened, and the House of Fire and Flame offered to take on the contract of clearing it.

Send for me.d: Graciana proposed restocking the Breadbasket with seed so the Keeper could send aid to a hungry territory or unsupplied army. This would need a vote of Marcher farm owners in Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold and a change to electing the Keeper by Tally of the Votes, and it would cost farm income. She suggested the Senate create titles to oversee other great works. Every region of Feroz was declared impoverished and abandoned; Morajasse and the Cazar Straits were lawless and underpopulated, as was Afarjasse. She offered four opportunities: replanting Bramar's fields, restoring the herds of Afar, building the Inkworks of Joharra and building the Oran Wharfage. A conjunction tasked the Strategos of the Brass Coast with defending the Celesti Lighthouse from Isidore i Boyaga's raiders.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Harps of Astolat are cited as a great work that might have helped the Empire had it had an overseeing title.
n.Grendel: Grendel rule of Feroz is blamed for its ruin. Rahab looted the territory, Quartermaster Maeve wrecked Bramar's fields and Maistir Fionnula sold off the herds of Afar, and former Grendel were among the wreckers raiding the lighthouse.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the herds of Afar are compared to the more celebrated great herd of Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; their only link is that Bregasland's Marcher farm owners were asked to vote on adapting the Breadbasket.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: most herb gardens are said to use companion-planting techniques the Navarr pioneered before the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn Feroz was found economically devastated and largely abandoned, with Graciana proposing commissions and new Brass Coast national titles to restore it. The Strategos of the Brass Coast, Gael i Guerra, was charged with saving the Celesti Lighthouse and could claim Isidore's ship, the Finder of Ways.
n.The Marches: Marcher farm owners were asked to vote on turning the Breadbasket into a tool for aiding devastated territories, at a cost to their own farm income. Their cattle-bonds could also help fund the restoration of the herds of Afar.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen architect Majorian of the Verdant Tower is recalled for his unfinished almanacs on companion planting.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Harps of Astolat are given as an example of a great work that might have aided the Empire with an overseer.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: wealth plundered from Feroz was shipped across the bay to the Broken Shore, and a wharfage would let Oran offer cheaper dock fees than elsewhere on the bay.
t.Bregasland: Its Marcher farm owners were among those asked to vote on adapting the Breadbasket to support struggling territories.
t.Feroz: Every region was declared impoverished and abandoned, so no Synod mandate affects the territory and its taxation cannot grow while any region is lawless. Civilian commissions there now cost one crown per wain, and several restoration opportunities were proposed.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Graciana is a native of Madruga who hopes to revive the friendly rivalry between Oran and Siroc.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: plans already proposed for Mareave's herds served as the model for restoring the herds of Afar, and the Shepherd of the Southern Herd is detailed in a companion wind.
t.Mitwold: Its Marcher farm owners were asked to vote on the Breadbasket change, and their cattle-bonds could help fund the herds of Afar.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Oath at Sunset, hakima from Cerevado, offered a Therasia's Chain each year to the Scrivener of the Inkworks.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's great herd is cited as more celebrated than the herds of Afar.
t.Upwold: The appraisal built on the Upwold Seed Exchange, and Upwold's farm owners were asked to vote on adapting the Breadbasket. Their cattle-bonds could also help fund the herds of Afar.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Afarjasse was found impoverished, abandoned and underpopulated after Maistir Fionnula sold off its herds. A 300-crown sinecure could restore them, create the Dhomiro of Afar to trade cattle with the Suranni of Arbonne and lift its impoverishment.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Under the Children of Wrecks the straits became lawless and underpopulated, and the Oran Wharfage was proposed as a way to end their lawlessness. Wreckers prowling these waters were raiding the Celesti Lighthouse.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The once-golden fields of Bramar were ruined under Quartermaster Maeve. If the Breadbasket were adapted, two seasons of its support could replant them and end the region's abandoned and impoverished state.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Morajasse was declared lawless and underpopulated, overrun by bandit groups. Only the area around Mora's Rock remains under the tight control of Gallum Fiersach.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Inkworks of Joharra, a great work, could revive the region's ruined dye trade and end its impoverishment, and the Oran Wharfage could be built at Oran. Wreckers were attacking the Celesti Lighthouse above Oran's cliffs.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Mentioned in passing: Lucksprings is not named on the page; Segura's only link is the Cerevado hakima supporting the inkworks.

So far so fast.d: After talks at Anvil in Autumn 386YE, the Lasambrians, with their three armies and Yantan Tethrasson's warband, offered to help reconquer Kahraman, Segura, Madruga and Feroz. In return the Empire would cede all of Segura, Gambit and Morajasse, with a six-month grace period for Freeborn residents. Other terms included a three-year mutual defence pact, free trade, Mercantile tariffs for the Faraden, perpetual Lasambrian neutrality between Empire and Jotun, and a three-year lease of the Damatian Cliffs. The civil service warned of losing the Iron Qanat and Freeborn army supply, the Iron Confederacy threat, and Cathan Canae's likely displeasure. The Lasambrians called it their final offer. The Senate rejected it.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish seneschal Chauntecleer Words asked the civil service how the Lady of the Frost might react to the treaty.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the civil service noted the Druj would react very badly to such negotiations, unlike the honour-bound Jotun.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held parts of Feroz and Madruga that the joint Imperial–Lasambrian campaign would have had to retake from them and the Children of Wrecks.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had agreed in principle to let the Lasambrians and their three armies leave the nation. Once the Senate rejected the treaty, the Lasambrians fought alongside the Jotun in the conquest of Bregasland.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn stood to see their whole coast reconquered but would lose Segura, Gambit and Morajasse. That would include the Iron Qanat, which was needed to supply their armies, as well as the Spice Gardens and the seat of the Incarnadine Satchel.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's joining of the Empire was cited as the kind of union the Lasambrians would never accept.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule armies were cited as earlier foreign orc allies of the Empire, and the Thule were said likely to react badly to such negotiations.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's joining of the Empire was cited as a path the Lasambrians would never follow.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Ossium alongside Thule armies was cited as a precedent for cooperating with foreign orcs.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Sermersuaq alongside Thule armies was cited as a precedent for cooperating with foreign orcs.

t.Bregasland: After the Senate rejected the treaty, the Lasambrians joined the Jotun in their conquest of Bregasland.
t.Feroz: Retaking Morajasse and the Cazar Straits was required under the treaty, but Morajasse would then have been ceded. The civil service noted that Feroz's underpopulation after Rahab's devastation worsened the Freeborn supply problem.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's joining of the Empire was cited as a union the Lasambrians would never emulate.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was wholly in Imperial hands, but its region of Gambit would have been ceded to Lasambria and the territory covered by the proposed defence pact.
t.Kalino: Kalino was held by the Iron Confederacy, who call it Arbonne. The Lasambrians still covet it, and the civil service warned they might one day seek Imperial backing to retake it.
t.Madruga: The joint campaign would have had to retake the Great Grasses, Free Landing and the Mysterious Swamp, and Lasambrian armies there would suffer attrition without supply lines back to Reinos.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium's conquest with Thule help was cited as a precedent for alliance with foreign orcs.
t.Reinos: Reinos was the Lasambrian homeland, where the treaty was debated in the Arena of Virtue, and it was to fall under the mutual defence pact. Once the treaty failed, the Empire invaded Reinos.
t.Segura: The whole territory would have been ceded, losing the Empire the Iron Qanat, the Cerevado Nets seat, the Towers of Anduz, the Faraden Embassy and substantial tax revenue.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's conquest with Thule help was cited as a precedent for alliance with foreign orcs.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Retaking the Cazar Straits was required by the treaty, but the Empire could not invade it without a navy.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Morajasse was to be reconquered and then ceded. That would have cost the Empire Mora's Rock, the Spice Gardens of Feroz and the offices of the Incarnadine Satchel.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: Gambit was to be ceded to the Lasambrians. Its Freeborn residents would have had six months to leave or to face the higher taxes paid by foreigners.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing had to be retaken under the treaty, but the Empire could not invade it without a navy, which risked Lasambrian accusations of bad faith.

Start a war.d: The Fangs, a thirteen-rock mithril mine in the Bitter Strand, fell into Imperial hands in poor repair: 16 wains a season for 20 thrones upkeep, with a possible 300-throne rebuild. Nineteen wains' worth of worked mithril arms became spoils for the Military Council. The Rahvin, about 500 strong, fled to the Carmine Fields with Irra Harah's help and vowed to retake the Fangs, facing destruction by Houndsgate unless ceded the land. The civil service raised a motion requiring fortifications to resist any attack, whatever its source. Archavion and his supporters were sentenced to death, and the Senate ceded the Bitter Strand to the Rahvin. A Dawnish Assembly veto was not upheld.

n.Dawn: Dawn was bitterly divided: Gryphons hailed Archavion for securing the Barrens and its mithril, while Unicorns, inspired by the Assembly's liberation crusade, wanted the Fangs ceded to the Rahvin. Archavion and his supporters were ultimately sentenced to death.
n.Druj: The Druj left a cruel legacy of slave cells at the Fangs. They were said to be spreading word of Imperial massacres to their subjects, undermining hopes that their slaves would rise against them.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn armies were noted as part of the Barrens liberation crusade, and several Highborn heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin flee.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: numerous Imperial Orc heroes are listed among those who supported the Rahvin's escape.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the weirwood groves of the Heart of Peytaht went to Navarr's allies the Great Forest Orcs, and Navarr heroes are listed among the Rahvin's supporters.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: two Freeborn heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin escape.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: some Dawnish resent Holberg going to the League, and League heroes are listed among the Rahvin's supporters.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: three members of the Hartell Household are listed among those who supported the Rahvin.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: four Urizen heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin flee.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Fangs' state is compared to Ossium's Sunless Depths, and Varushkan heroes are listed among the Rahvin's supporters.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: several Wintermark heroes are listed among those who helped the Rahvin escape.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Rahvin sheltered in caves in the Carmine Fields near the Holberg border, and some Dawnish grumble that Holberg should have been theirs.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Fangs' cruel, ill-built workings recall the state of Ossium's Sunless Depths when they were claimed.
t.The Barrens: Support for the attack on the Rahvin was strongest here. The territory's newest mithril mine passed into Imperial hands, and the expelled Rahvin vowed to retake it at once.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish noble cites the Druj having just destroyed two armies in Therunin as a reason to press the war.
t.Weirwater: Opposition to the attack on the Rahvin, and support for the Unicorns' call for peace, was strongest in Weirwater.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Fangs mine lies here, its abandoned Rahvin tools and worked mithril now Imperial spoils. The Senate ultimately voted to cede the Bitter Strand to the Rahvin.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Mentioned in passing: its weirwood groves were given to the Great Forest Orcs, a sore point for Dawnish who felt denied the spoils of war.

The long road.d: For four summits no one could challenge Barien. Once the conjunction passed, the ritual returned in a changed form: the Iron Duke now sets the contests, and willing challengers need a coven to cast Challenge the Iron Duke on them. The Challenge of the Endless Sea, offered through Rhianos' herald Latitude, has crews of four hunting the metal-skinned Adamantilus in the Gosgala chamber. The Challenge of the Frayed Pennant pits ten Imperial combatants against ten Jotun, led by Kjellaug Spearbiter and Oddmund Gunnesbarn, in a pennant-capture battle at the Emerald Glade in Southridge, Hahnmark. Those who yield must be spared. The winners may each choose an item from the Dragonforge, and extra prizes are offered.

n.Jotun: Two Jotun champions, Kjellaug Spearbiter of Kierheim and Oddmund Gunnesbarn of Fjorknae, have challenged the Empire to the Frayed Pennant battle and are raising a team of ten. Their priest Brynta welcomes the return of Barien's challenges as a way for restless newcomers to prove themselves.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the only possible link is the Steelskin prize, a Knightly Redoubt armour.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Frayed Pennant contest is staged at the Emerald Glade in Southridge, Hahnmark, a Wintermark territory.

t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: Oddmund Gunnesbarn, one of the two Jotun champions in the Frayed Pennant challenge, is described as hailing from far-flung Fjorknae.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is the venue for the Challenge of the Frayed Pennant. Imperial and Jotun teams, with up to 80 spectators, are to fight a mock battle there under Barien's heralds.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not referred to; the word appears only in the name of the Knightly Redoubt armour offered as the Steelskin prize.

r.Hahnmark/Southridge: The Emerald Glade in Southridge hosts the Frayed Pennant battle. Two teams of ten will defend menhirs in a patch of woodland and try to seize each other's pennants, and anyone who yields must be spared.

The war of thorns and flowers.d: With the grey pilgrims home, Highguard could support a fourth army, but the pilgrims refused to serve under the Thundering Tide's name. Banners hallowed with true liao could cut its mithril cost. Virtue's Rest in Bastion could become an army resupply hostel. Else Van Temeschwar proposed tolls on the Empire's major roads, and Varushka was offered sovereign patrons, Irontooth Keep and a Winter-aligned Icy Crag. In the outcome, four banners were hallowed, saving 120 wains, the Pilgrim's Defiance was commissioned, Virtue's Rest was remodelled, and tolls on the Blood Red and White Roads raised 100 thrones a season. Irontooth Keep and the Icy Crag were not taken up.

n.Dawn: Larkin Shrike's call for a War of Thorns and Flowers passed 282-64 without a greater majority, so the nation was not yet committed. Separately, the Knight of the Greenwood was asked to recover Druj herb caches in Brocéliande.
n.Druj: Kaela's Gift let captured Imperial citizens die painlessly beyond their reach. Druj herb caches abandoned in Brocéliande might be reclaimed if Imperial knights failed to recover them.
n.Highguard: The returning grey pilgrims allowed a fourth Highborn army, which they refused to raise under the Thundering Tide's name. Highguard hallowed four banners with true liao, commissioned the Pilgrim's Defiance and remodelled Virtue's Rest.
n.Navarr: Navarr's war on the vallorn was the cause other nations rallied to or refused, with Wintermark declining to support it. Navarr armies were eligible to resupply at Virtue's Rest, and Deer's Folly sought the Spear of the Seven's help against a vallornspawn horde.
n.The Brass Coast: The Sunset Roads were included in the toll proposal and the Freeborn Assembly could have vetoed it, but in the end only the Blood Red and White Roads were tolled. Varushkan armies no longer suffered a penalty for fighting alongside Freeborn armies unless the Freeborn Assembly renewed its concerns.
n.The League: The League Assembly committed its citizens' ambition and ingenuity to the vallorn war, so its other statements of principle would have no effect for a year. Else Van Temeschwar's road-toll scheme led to tolls on the Blood Red and White Roads.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were named as a possible future threat to Suvretz, one reason to build Irontooth Keep, and the vallornheart in Sküld lies across the border.
n.Urizen: Eurydice Starchaser's statement backing the Navarr's magical army in Miaren passed 150-0 but without a greater majority, so Urizen remained uncommitted despite the threat from Therunin's vallorn.
n.Varushka: Varushka committed to the vallorn war, locking its Assembly's other causes for a year. It could support two more armies and was offered sovereign patronage, Irontooth Keep and a Winter-aligned Icy Crag, though the last two were not taken up. The penalty for fighting beside Freeborn or Wintermark armies was lifted.
n.Wintermark: Ingrid Talon-of-the-Mark's statement that Wintermark cannot support the Navarr above every other threat passed with a greater majority but gave no clear call to action. The Runegrott in Northspires was threatened by a vallornspawn horde.

t.Bastion: Virtue's Rest was remodelled into hostels where eligible armies can resupply, at the cost of its investment and liao returns, and the title Exarch of Virtue's Rest was created.
t.Brocéliande: Knights-errant found abandoned Druj herb caches amid the vallornspawn, and the Knight of the Greenwood was asked to recover them. Kaela's Gift extends into the territory.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: its Silent Sentinel was cited as the kind of major fortification Irontooth Keep might rival.
t.Hahnmark: A vallornspawn horde from Hercynia threatened to cross into Northspires and attack the Runegrott and its artisans.
t.Hercynia: A horde of vallornspawn husks led by a huge chitinous monster moved through Deer's Folly towards the Northspires border, and the Spear of the Seven was asked to stop it.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Kamkrags of Kahraman were excluded from the road-toll proposal on constitutional grounds.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is not named directly and is touched only through wider Varushkan matters such as the debate over tolling the nation's roads.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly and is touched only through the wider proposal to toll Freeborn roads, which was not adopted.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's statement called for support for the magical army the Navarr planned to raise in Miaren.
t.Miekarova: The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun could have been realigned from Summer to Winter magic with Cabalist funding, but the opportunity was not taken.
t.Otkodov: The vallornheart in Sküld is the one nearest Varushka, and its forests run unbroken into Suvretz.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: its fortification Remember Exile was cited as a benchmark for Irontooth Keep.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the opening vignette is set in Temeschwar, where accountant Else Van Temeschwar is confronted over her road-toll recommendations.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the loss of Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms there was recalled, its vallorn was noted as a threat to Urizen, and Kaela's Gift extends there.
t.Volodmartz: A rank 2 fortification, Irontooth Keep, was proposed for Suvretz to guard against the vallorn and the Thule, but it was not built.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The Order of the Emerald Dogs came out of Dark Ranging with reports of scattered Druj and abandoned herb stockpiles overrun by vallornspawn.
r.Hahnmark/Northspires: The Runegrott, the region's most substantial construction, was at risk if the vallornspawn horde crossed the border, drawing the interest of its Keeper, Derowen.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: The western steadings faced abandonment unless the Spear of the Seven stopped the advancing vallornspawn horde.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun here could have become a college of Winter magic, but this was not done.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Its vallornheart threatened to spill through the forests into Suvretz if the hearts were linked.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: Suvretz was offered Irontooth Keep, a quickly built fortress on old ruins, against vallorn from Sküld and future Thule attack, but it was not commissioned.

Theory of the crows.d: Asavea's Plenum rebuffed Sarcophan protests over its bounty on ships trading with the Empire. In response the Delves proposed the Free Seas Pact: signatories would bar pirates, place no bounties on other signatories' ships except in war, and embargo any nation that refused to sign. Negotiator Johann Van Basten was sent to Anvil to agree terms with Ambassador Dino i Riqueza. Sarcophan escorts were keeping trade routes open for now, but not indefinitely. Other matters included revised Kruidenkenner herb deliveries, the Alivetti Estates, a raised offer for white granite, vlinderbloem farming in Wintermark, meetings with Elian Vlas and the Lijkkever, puzzlement over the Barrens, and a warning about the Elakar.

n.Dawn: Elian Vlas proposed meeting Imperial officials at the Wise Guise in Dawn, and the Community of Silence had engaged a renowned Dawnish artist from Astolat to decorate their temple.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj being in retreat is cited as one reason the Delves now take an interest in trade with Holberg.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan presence at Crown's Quay in Necropolis is noted as a possible cheaper site for the Bladgoud Tuiniers' business.
n.The League: League cities drew Sarcophan interest: the Lijkkever sent Schuyler Koopman to meet Holberg's Chamber of Commerce, and the Bladgoud Tuiniers sought buyers for their legal drugs in Sarvos or would leave. Elian Vlas also hoped to visit League theatres.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Urizen directly.
n.Varushka: Varushka's Ivarsgard in Karsk is described as the closest Sarcophan trade hub to the Barrens and a place with an established Sarcophan presence.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark farmers had harvested their first vlinderbloem crop for the Kraft brothers in exchange for viezesmaak. The brothers invited Wintermark merchants to propose further trade.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: a renowned Dawnish artist from Astolat had been offered to the Community of Silence to decorate their temple.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: in the opening fiction the Asavean envoy refers to Imperials as the 'assassins of Catazar'.
t.Hahnmark: The first Imperially grown vlinderbloem was ready to harvest, and the resulting viezesmaak was shared with Hahnmark's farmers, with most of it exported.
t.Holberg: With the Barrens no longer hostile, the Lijkkever's Schuyler Koopman planned to come to Anvil to explore trade with Holberg's Chamber of Commerce. Annike declined the invitation to its 250th anniversary celebration.
t.Karsk: Ivarsgard in Karsk was named as the nearest Sarcophan trade hub to the Barrens and a possible site for the Bladgoud Tuiniers to set up shop.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay in Necropolis is noted as having a Sarcophan presence that could lower setup costs for the Bladgoud Tuiniers.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page.
t.Sarvos: After the Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce declined their offer, the Bladgoud Tuiniers' handelsschool was failing. Aaven Beekhof sought buyers for their legal drugs, warning they would probably leave Sarvos by the Spring Equinox without a convincing offer.
t.The Barrens: Annike was baffled by the Ambassador's reassurance about General Archavion's actions in the Barrens, since the Delves had no interests there. She allowed that a port on the Barren Sea would interest them if the territory proved rich in resources.

Under eastern skies.d: The Black Thorns, Iron Helms, Golden Sun and Isaella's Dance advanced into Eastring and found themselves outnumbered and caught in a Druj ward. The vengeful Black Wind led a merciless onslaught. Isaella's Dance gave their lives to break the ward, then the Iron Helms, aided by Winter spirits and their own risen dead, cut a path north into the Bleaks. Some twelve and a half thousand Imperial soldiers were lost and both armies disbanded. The Druj hold Eastring and East Ashes, and Therunin stays uncontrolled. Opportunities followed: binding the undead Helms, recovering lost regalia, and making a corpse glade at Isaella's Fall.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun lost about a thousand soldiers, and Eleonaris' knights died fighting beside them. The Druj offered to enslave surrendering Dawnish, and Lady Laudine du Lac was asked to lead questing knights against Druj traders in the Salt Flats.
n.Druj: The Druj sprang their trap, destroyed two Imperial armies and recaptured Eastring, though they surely lost thousands to the furious Varushkans. The Tainted Basilisk has left Therunin, which denies them large-scale rituals there.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a quoted Prosperity Assembly judgement names the Grendel among raiders stealing the Empire's prosperity.
n.Navarr: Isaella's Dance was wiped out and around two thousand Black Thorns died. The nation is offered the chance to recover the Knife of Thorns standard and to braid its dead with the Great Forest Orcs in a corpse glade at Isaella's Fall.
n.The League: The Towerjacks had fortified Peakedge Song before leaving to help defend Redoubt. Their weakened defences remain until the Spring Equinox.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle marched south into Urizen to aid the defence of Redoubt.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms were destroyed and the Northern Eagle lost some two hundred in the Lower Tarn Valley. Varushka may bind the risen Helms with a hearth rite at the Stained Rock, or recover the Barrow Axe to bargain with a sovereign.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Isaella's Dance had recuperated in Astolat the previous season before marching to Therunin.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, a painless death for Imperial citizens held by the Druj, extends into Brocéliande.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Wagon raiders asked Champion of Prosperity Hugh Farrier to kill Druj guards so they could loot a weirwood shipment. Success would reward him with four wains of weirwood and encourage further raids.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Malinov family of Karsk holds the artefact axe Hunger and refused to return it to the Iron Helms.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Varnalis homestead targeted by wagon raiders lies just across the border from Ossium's Drownbark Forest.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks and Northern Eagle left Therunin to aid Redoubt's defence.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Dawnish questing knights tracked Druj carrying goods to the Dripping Market and asked Lady Laudine du Lac to kill them and claim their wares.
t.Sarangrave: A coven of human Winter ritualists from eastern Sarangrave, the Krollthorned, was aiding the Druj. If Varushka binds the dead Iron Helms, they could be sent to ravage Sarangrave and prevent Druj resupply there.
t.Therunin: Imperial forces lost some twelve and a half thousand soldiers here, and Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms were destroyed. The Druj retook Eastring and the territory remains uncontrolled, with a Spring curse fouling the land and the undead Helms roaming its marshes.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: The Varnalis, a Druj family of Grimfen Mire, were expecting a weirwood shipment that wagon raiders planned to seize after killing its guards.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Mentioned in passing: the Druj homestead targeted by raiders lies just across the border from Drownbark Forest.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Beladrarsh: The Skinweavers of Beladrarsh host the Dripping Market, the destination of the Druj traders the Dawnish knights were hunting.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Mentioned in passing: the Krollthorned coven likely serves a ghulai allied to the Palace of the Sleepers in northern Kroll.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: The Druj still hold East Ashes, giving them both shores of the Feverwater, and protect it with a malign Spring ward. A captured Great Forest Orc treetender was being forced to work rafts on the Feverwater's edge.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring was the killing ground where a Druj ward trapped the Imperial armies, and the Druj recaptured it. The risen dead of the Iron Helms now roam its marshes, and Isaella's Fall lies here.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: Greenheart remains under the control of the vallorn.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Still held by the Navarr, the valley lies poisoned by the Sephals Cauldron, worsened by the Druj curse. Some two hundred Northern Eagle soldiers died crossing it, and the trapped armies dared not retreat through it.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Still held by the Navarr, Peakedge Song kept the Towerjacks' fortifications around its hospital. Displaced Navarr and Great Forest Orcs gathered at Peakedge Stead.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: Sweetglades remains under the control of the vallorn.

Wasp nest.d: Hazelelponi's statement of principle passed by greater majority, the last use of this peerless kinship. With Eastring under the Druj, the Highborn and Navarr planned the Glade of Farewell, a weirwood memorial to be built and consecrated once a ravaged region is Imperial and uncorrupted. Samples of the Sephals Cauldron poison were brought to Anvil to find an antidote, which could then be applied through the Senate, the Gardens of High Chalcis or a suitable army. Other opportunities were the Micah's Stand wayhouse and a fortification for Peakedge Song. The briars have left the Garden of Glory, so its Keeper now receives twelve liao. The Assembly might seek to make peerless kinship permanent, at a cost.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: wounded Dawnish soldiers suggested the Barrens' shrine of hope as a model, and past kinship work had aided the Dawnish in the Barrens.
n.Druj: The Druj hold Eastring and East Ashes, where ghosts linger. They poisoned the Lower Tarn Valley, the Black Wind are eager to seize Imperial priests, and Peakedge Stead is feared to be their next target.
n.Highguard: Highborn priests and magisters led the effort to aid Navarr, bringing poison samples to Anvil and proposing a memorial glade and a fortification. This was their last chance to express peerless kinship, though they may seek to keep it permanently at a cost.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn kinship work helped the Imperial Orcs in Skarsind understand the Ossium septs.
n.Navarr: The Navarr gained Highborn help with Therunin's restless dead, a plan to cure the poisoned Lower Tarn and a possible wayhouse and Keeper title for displaced Navarr in Reikos. Their herbalists also took over the abandoned Garden of Glory.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn kinship work aided the Freeborn in Kahraman.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: past Highborn kinship work helped the Marches deal with threats in the Mournwold.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is cited as a place where the Druj once broke captured priests and turned them against the Empire.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn work sought to increase understanding of the Ossium septs.
n.Wintermark: The Blood Cloaks were named as one of the few armies with the expertise to clear the Lower Tarn poison in a single season, if protected by Why Sulemaine Walked Away From The Baker.

t.Brocéliande: The proposed Keeper of the Stand would be charged with working to reclaim Vale's Lament from the vallorn.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: listed among the places where earlier Highborn kinship aided the Freeborn.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus is engaged in its liberation, and earlier Highborn kinship helped the Marches there.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: cited as a haunted place whose ghosts give the Highborn their expertise with unquiet dead.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: earlier kinship work sought to increase understanding of the Ossium septs.
t.Reikos: Reikos could host the Micah's Stand wayhouse, and the Benefactor of High Chalcis could redirect the Gardens' herbs to cleanse Therunin, at the cost of the territory's herb yields while the work lasted.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: earlier Highborn kinship work with the Imperial Orcs took place there.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: its shrine of hope inspired the glade plan, and it is cited as a place where the Druj once turned captured priests.
t.Therunin: Therunin's war-haunted east, poisoned Lower Tarn Valley and vulnerable Peakedge Stead are the focus of the opportunities offered: a memorial glade, an antidote campaign and a possible fortification.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj once broke captured priests and turned them against the Empire.

r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: The proposed Keeper of the Stand would be charged with striving to free Vale's Lament from the vallorn.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Micah's Stand could be built in Chalcis Mount before the Summer Solstice 387YE, creating the Keeper of the Stand title and boosting the herb yield of the Gardens of High Chalcis.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: Conquered East Ashes holds unquiet spirits and is a possible site for the Glade of Farewell, but only once it is liberated.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring is haunted by many of the slaughtered dead but firmly Druj-held. Any priestly work must wait for its liberation, though the Glade of Farewell would at minimum lay its ghosts to rest.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are judged very unlikely to attack through the vallorn of Greenheart.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Imperial-held but poisoned valley could be cleansed if an antidote is found, through the Senate, the Gardens of High Chalcis or an army. Its abandoned Garden of Glory now yields twelve liao to its Keeper but remains under threat.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Stead, its hospital and the new apothecary college are left undefended, and the Highborn urge a fortification built of white granite or weirwood.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: the Garden of Glory lies on its edge, and the Highborn fear abominations could pour out of it.

Watching you well.d: Following a unanimous Autumn Equinox 386YE direction from the Assembly of Nine, the Silent Bell questioned Suranni magicians rescued into the Empire and lawkeepers at the Suranni embassy in Sarvos. They described the disunited cult as made up of downtrodden members, diabolists, opportunists and murderous aberrants, the last likely being those freed from Axiom Prison by the Children of Wrecks. Most members see the Empire as an ally against the Dukes and have barely resisted the 384YE ban, which is punished with fines. The Bell outlined options for the Senate, Synod and Conclave to act, but warned that confronting the cult more effectively would likely provoke curses, kidnappings, subversion and violence.

n.The League: The League's Assembly of Nine commissioned the investigation unanimously, and League interest in the Black Plateau was answered with the finding that no connection to the Hand of Dumon could be found.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos is home to the Suranni embassy, whose lawkeepers told the Silent Bell that they are reluctant to execute aberrants, which led the Bell to conclude that aberrants made up most of those freed from Axiom Prison.

Weird Goodbye.d: After Imperial heroes slew two Jotun warbands tracking the Artok, Big Icebarn was marked with Hirmok and Jotra and Little Icebarn with Hirmok and Pallas. The Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, Liv Tidgaring, could send Big Icebarn raiding into Jotun Skallahn or Tromsa, or hunting monsters and beasts in Sermersuaq. The Keeper of the Runegrott, Derowen, could set Little Icebarn to mining or to building commissions. Big Icebarn went hunting, which would aid Wintermark units fighting monsters there and could continue if supported by a thousand strength. Little Icebarn went mining, adding four wains of mithril a season to the Pride for a year.

n.Jotun: The Jotun lost two warbands that had been tracking the Artok, and they escaped Big Icebarn being unleashed into Kalsea to distract their jarls, because it was sent hunting instead.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's title-holders chose how to use the two Artok. Their military units gained help against the monsters of Sermersuaq, and the nation gained extra mithril from the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

t.Sermersuaq: Big Icebarn was set to draw out and kill the monsters of Agramant in the Suaq wastes, easing the work of Wintermark units hunting there. It would only remain next season if they supported it with a thousand strength.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was one of the Jotun territories where Big Icebarn could have been sent to distract the jarls and aid Wintermark raiders, but that option was not chosen.
t.Tromsa: Tromsa was one of the Jotun territories where Big Icebarn could have been sent to cause destruction and distraction, but the Artok was sent hunting in Sermersuaq instead.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Little Icebarn was set to claw out ore from dangerous, inaccessible veins at the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Suaq Fount, increasing the mine's output by four wains of mithril a season for a year.
